meta.dialect: Rigol DHO800/DHO900 subset with OOS extensions

intro: This chapter describes every command OOS Plus implements, grouped by subsystem. Commands marked **OOS** are extensions that the Rigol DHO800/DHO900 command set does not have. Commands not listed here are not supported and report error -113.

subsystems.title: IEEE 488.2 Common Commands
subsystems.intro: The IEEE 488.2 common commands identify the instrument, restore the default setup, and handle the error queue, the Standard Event Status Register and operation-complete synchronisation. OOS implements the subset listed here; there is no Status Byte, Service Request or event-enable register.

commands.desc: Queries the identification string of the instrument.
remarks: - The reply identifies OOS, not the stock firmware. Scripts that test for a Rigol manufacturer string must be adapted.
- The header is answered with or without the `?`, so a bare `*IDN` also produces a reply.
- The serial field is `0` when the platform does not report a serial number.
commands.returns: The query returns `OOS,<model>,<serial>,oos-ui <version>`, where `<model>` is the model name of the instrument and `<version>` is the OOS software version.
commands.example: *IDN?    /*The query returns OOS,DHO924S,0,oos-ui 0.1.5.*/

commands.desc: Restores the instrument to its default setup, as the front-panel **Default** key does.
remarks: - Clears the Standard Event Status Register and any pending `*OPC` registrations before the default setup is applied.
- The default setup is the application's own default and can differ between platforms.
- `*RST?` is not supported and generates error `-113,"Undefined header"`; the reset is not performed.
commands.example: *RST    /*Restores the default setup.*/

commands.desc: Clears the error queue, the Standard Event Status Register and all pending `*OPC` event registrations.
remarks: - Waveform memory, references and measurement results are not affected.
- `*CLS?` is not supported.
commands.example: *CLS    /*Clears the error queue and the event status register.*/

commands.desc: Queries and clears the Standard Event Status Register.
remarks: - Reading the register clears it.

- Implemented bits: bit 0 (1) Operation Complete, bit 2 (4) Query Error (-4xx), bit 3 (8) Device-Specific Error (-3xx, including queue overflow -350 and buffer overrun -363), bit 4 (16) Execution Error (-2xx and any code outside -100 to -499), bit 5 (32) Command Error (-1xx).
- There is no power-on bit and no event-enable register (`*ESE` is not implemented).
commands.returns: The query returns the register value as a decimal integer from `0` to `255`.
commands.example: *ESR?    /*The query returns 32 after a command error.*/

commands.desc: The command registers an operation-complete event that sets bit 0 of the Standard Event Status Register when the operations pending at that moment finish. The query returns `1` once those operations have finished.
remarks: - Only finite operations are waited for: an Autoset in progress, a submitted SIM record generation, and an armed Single acquisition. Continuous Run and background measurement, Math, decode and eye calculations are not waited for.
- The query must be sent as the exact text `*OPC?` (case-insensitive); it is evaluated in sequence with the other commands of the same program message.

- Over raw TCP and HiSLIP the reply is deferred until completion without blocking other clients. The synchronous HTTP interface cannot defer a reply and generates error `-221,"Operation pending; use raw TCP or HiSLIP for *OPC?"` while an operation is pending.
- If the awaited operation is cancelled or re-armed, no `1` is sent, the rest of the program message is discarded and error `-410,"OPC query interrupted by cancelled operation"` is queued.
- At most 64 `*OPC` registrations can be pending; a further `*OPC` generates error `-350,"Too many pending OPC events"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `1`.
commands.example: :SING;*OPC?    /*Arms a single acquisition; the query returns 1 when it has completed.*/

subsystems.title: Root Commands (Acquisition Control)
subsystems.intro: The root commands start, stop and force acquisitions, run Autoset and clear the display. They act on the live inputs or, when a reference is the trigger source, on the stored-record acquisition.

commands.desc: Starts the acquisition.
remarks: - `:RUN` sets the Run state; it is not a toggle, so repeating it has no further effect.
- With live inputs, a Single sweep is changed to Auto.
- When a reference is the trigger source (stored-record acquisition, including SIM records), a Single sweep is changed to Normal and an acquisition that is already running is left untouched.
- `:RUN?` is not supported.
commands.example: :RUN    /*Starts the acquisition.*/

commands.desc: Stops the acquisition.
remarks: - `:STOP` sets the Stop state; it is not a toggle.
- While a SIM record is being generated, `:STOP` cancels the generation.
- In stored-record acquisition, `:STOP` sent while already stopped also turns SIM playback off.
- `:STOP?` is not supported.
commands.example: :STOP    /*Stops the acquisition.*/

commands.desc: Sets the trigger sweep to Single and arms one acquisition, after which the instrument stops.
remarks: - Each `:SINGle` starts a new operation that `*OPC?` waits for, so `:SING;*OPC?` returns `1` when the capture is complete.
- `:SINGle?` is not supported.
commands.example: :SING    /*Arms a single acquisition.*/

commands.desc: Forces one acquisition without waiting for the trigger condition, as the front-panel **Force** key does.
remarks: - Use it to release a Normal or Single sweep when the trigger condition never occurs.
- With live inputs, the hardware is asked for one forced trigger; in stored-record acquisition, the record is replayed with a software force.
commands.example: :TFOR    /*Generates a forced trigger.*/

commands.desc: Starts Autoset, as the front-panel **Auto** key does. The query reports whether Autoset is in progress.
remarks: - Autoset adjusts the live inputs only; it does not fit a reference.
- Autoset is a finite operation: `:AUT;*OPC?` returns `1` when it has finished.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` while Autoset is running, otherwise `0`.
commands.example:
:AUT     /*Starts Autoset.*/
:AUT?    /*The query returns 0 when Autoset has finished.*/

commands.desc: Clears the display persistence and the measurement statistics, as the front-panel **Clear** key does.
remarks: - `:CLEar?` is not supported.
commands.example: :CLE    /*Clears persistence and measurement statistics.*/

subsystems.title: :ACQuire Commands
subsystems.intro: The :ACQuire commands set the acquisition type, average count, memory depth and segmented-frame count, and query the sample rate.

commands.desc: Queries the current sample rate in Sa/s.
remarks: - The value is the acquisition rate of the instrument for the current time base and channel configuration, not the native rate of a loaded reference.
- The set form is not supported and generates error `-113,"Undefined header"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the sample rate in scientific notation, for example `1.250000E+09`.
commands.example: :ACQ:SRAT?    /*The query returns 1.250000E+09.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the memory depth, the number of points stored per channel in one acquisition.
remarks: - `<depth>` can be written as a plain number (for example `1000000`) or with a `K` or `M` suffix (for example `1M`, `62.5M`). The value must be exactly one of the listed depths; it is not rounded to the nearest one.
- Any argument that begins with `AUTO` selects automatic depth.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-113,"Undefined header"` followed by the command text.
commands.returns: The query returns the effective memory depth in points in scientific notation, for example `1.000000E+06`. A number is returned even when AUTO is selected.
commands.example:
:ACQ:MDEP 1M     /*Sets the memory depth to 1 Mpts.*/
:ACQ:MDEP?       /*The query returns 1.000000E+06.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the acquisition type.
remarks: - NORMal: sampling at equal intervals. PEAK: peak detect, keeping the minimum and maximum of each interval. AVERages: averages successive acquisitions; the count is set with `:ACQuire:AVERages`. HRESolution: high resolution, averaging adjacent samples.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns `NORM`, `PEAK`, `AVER` or `HRES`.
commands.example:
:ACQ:TYPE AVER    /*Selects the average acquisition type.*/
:ACQ:TYPE?        /*The query returns AVER.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the number of averages used when the acquisition type is AVERages.
remarks: - A value that is not a power of 2 is rounded down to the next lower power of 2; values above 1024 give 1024.
- A non-integer value or a value below 2 is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the count as an integer, for example `64`.
commands.example:
:ACQ:AVER 64    /*Sets the average count to 64.*/
:ACQ:AVER?      /*The query returns 64.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the number of frames kept in segmented memory.
remarks: - Any non-negative integer is accepted and snapped to the nearest listed value. `0` turns segmented memory off.
- This sets the segment count only; it does not imply the capture rate of the stock UltraAcquire mode.
- A value that is not a non-negative integer generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the frame count as an integer, for example `100`.
commands.example:
:ACQ:ULTR:MAXF 100    /*Keeps 100 frames in segmented memory.*/
:ACQ:ULTR:MAXF?       /*The query returns 100.*/

subsystems.title: :CHANnel Commands
subsystems.intro: The :CHANnel commands set the vertical system of each analog input: display, scale, offset, coupling, bandwidth limit, probe ratio, inversion, units, labels and deskew. Vertical values are expressed at the probe tip, so they include the probe ratio.

commands.desc: Turns the specified channel on or off, or queries its state.
remarks: - `<n>` accepts 1 to 4 whatever the number of inputs of the connected model; any other value generates error `-113,"Undefined header"`.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-113,"Undefined header"` followed by the command text.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` or `0`.
commands.example:
:CHAN2:DISP ON    /*Turns CH2 on.*/
:CHAN2:DISP?      /*The query returns 1.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the vertical scale of the specified channel, in units per division at the probe tip.
remarks: - The scale steps follow a 1-2-5 sequence from 100 µV/div to 10 V/div multiplied by the probe ratio (for a 10X probe: 1 mV/div to 100 V/div). A value between steps is set to the nearest step; zero or a negative value selects the smallest step.
- Setting the scale resets the fine (vernier) factor of the channel to 1.
- When the vertical expansion reference is GND (`:CHANnel<n>:EXPand GND`), the offset is rescaled in proportion so the trace keeps its position relative to ground.
- The query returns the effective scale, including the probe ratio and any fine adjustment.
- `<n>` accepts 1 to 4 whatever the number of inputs of the connected model; any other value generates error `-113,"Undefined header"`.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-113,"Undefined header"` followed by the command text.
commands.returns: The query returns the vertical scale in scientific notation, for example `5.000000E-01`.
commands.example:
:CHAN1:SCAL 0.5    /*Sets the vertical scale of CH1 to 500 mV/div.*/
:CHAN1:SCAL?       /*The query returns 5.000000E-01.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the vertical offset of the specified channel, in volts.
remarks: - The value is not limited to a range; any finite number is accepted.
- `:CHANnel<n>:POSition` is an exact alias of OFFSet and also takes volts, not divisions.
- `<n>` accepts 1 to 4 whatever the number of inputs of the connected model; any other value generates error `-113,"Undefined header"`.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-113,"Undefined header"` followed by the command text.
commands.returns: The query returns the offset in scientific notation, for example `-1.500000E+00`.
commands.example:
:CHAN1:OFFS -1.5    /*Sets the vertical offset of CH1 to -1.5 V.*/
:CHAN1:OFFS?       /*The query returns -1.500000E+00.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the input coupling of the specified channel.
remarks: - DC passes both the DC and AC components; AC blocks the DC component; GND disconnects the signal.
- The tokens must be written in full (case-insensitive). `DC50` (50 Ω input) is accepted only on hardware that provides it; the DHO800/900 does not.
- `<n>` accepts 1 to 4 whatever the number of inputs of the connected model; any other value generates error `-113,"Undefined header"`.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-113,"Undefined header"` followed by the command text.
commands.returns: The query returns `DC`, `AC`, `GND` or `DC50`.
commands.example:
:CHAN1:COUP AC    /*Selects AC coupling for CH1.*/
:CHAN1:COUP?      /*The query returns AC.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the bandwidth limit of the specified channel.
remarks: - OFF and FULL select full bandwidth. AUTO lets the filter follow the sample rate. 20M (or 20MHZ) selects the 20 MHz limit.

- `<filter>` selects one of the instrument's filters by its frequency, written without spaces, with or without the `HZ` suffix: 5M, 10M, 15M, 25M, 30M, 35M, 40M, 50M, 60M, 70M, 75M, 80M, 90M, 100M, 125M, 150M, 175M, 200M, 250M, 300M, 310M, 400M, 600M, 800M, 1G, 1.5G, 2G (for example `100M` or `100MHZ`, `1G` or `1GHZ`).
- `GND` is also accepted and selects the GND entry of the bandwidth menu.
- `<n>` accepts 1 to 4 whatever the number of inputs of the connected model; any other value generates error `-113,"Undefined header"`.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-113,"Undefined header"` followed by the command text.
commands.returns: The query returns `OFF` (full bandwidth), `AUTO`, `20M`, `GND`, or the filter frequency in upper case without spaces, for example `100MHZ` or `1GHZ`.
commands.example:
:CHAN1:BWL 20M    /*Limits the bandwidth of CH1 to 20 MHz.*/
:CHAN1:BWL?       /*The query returns 20M.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the probe attenuation ratio of the specified channel.
remarks: - The ratio is not restricted to a list of standard values.
- The vertical scale, offset and measurement results are expressed at the probe tip, so they follow the probe ratio.
- Zero or a negative value is not applied.
- `<n>` accepts 1 to 4 whatever the number of inputs of the connected model; any other value generates error `-113,"Undefined header"`.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-113,"Undefined header"` followed by the command text.
commands.returns: The query returns the probe ratio in scientific notation, for example `1.000000E+01`.
commands.example:
:CHAN1:PROB 10    /*Sets the probe ratio of CH1 to 10X.*/
:CHAN1:PROB?      /*The query returns 1.000000E+01.*/

commands.desc: Turns waveform inversion of the specified channel on or off, or queries its state.
remarks: - `<n>` accepts 1 to 4 whatever the number of inputs of the connected model; any other value generates error `-113,"Undefined header"`.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-113,"Undefined header"` followed by the command text.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` or `0`.
commands.example:
:CHAN1:INV ON    /*Inverts the CH1 waveform.*/
:CHAN1:INV?      /*The query returns 1.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the amplitude unit of the specified channel.
remarks: - The unit changes how values are labelled; it does not rescale the data.
- `<n>` accepts 1 to 4 whatever the number of inputs of the connected model; any other value generates error `-113,"Undefined header"`.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns `VOLT`, `AMP`, `WATT` or `UNKN`.
commands.example:
:CHAN2:UNIT AMP    /*Sets the unit of CH2 to amperes.*/
:CHAN2:UNIT?       /*The query returns AMP.*/

commands.desc: Turns fine adjustment of the vertical scale on or off, or queries its state.
remarks: - There is one fine-adjust switch shared by all channels; the setting and the query are the same whichever `<n>` is used.
- Turning it OFF resets the fine factor of channel `<n>` to 1, returning that channel to a calibrated 1-2-5 step.
- `<n>` accepts 1 to 4 whatever the number of inputs of the connected model; any other value generates error `-113,"Undefined header"`.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` or `0`.
commands.example:
:CHAN1:VERN ON    /*Turns fine vertical adjustment on.*/
:CHAN1:VERN?      /*The query returns 1.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the vertical expansion reference, the point the waveform expands or compresses around when the vertical scale changes.
remarks: - GND: the waveform expands around its ground level. CENTer: the waveform expands around the screen centre.
- There is one expansion reference shared by all channels; `<n>` does not select a separate setting.
- `<n>` accepts 1 to 4 whatever the number of inputs of the connected model; any other value generates error `-113,"Undefined header"`.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns `GND` or `CENT`.
commands.example:
:CHAN1:EXP GND    /*Expands the waveforms around ground.*/
:CHAN1:EXP?       /*The query returns GND.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the zero-bias correction of the specified channel, in volts.
remarks: - The correction is subtracted in software from the channel reading, for example to cancel the zero error of a current probe.
- `<n>` accepts 1 to 4 whatever the number of inputs of the connected model; any other value generates error `-113,"Undefined header"`.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns the correction in scientific notation, for example `2.000000E-03`.
commands.example:
:CHAN1:BIAS 0.002    /*Subtracts 2 mV from the CH1 reading.*/
:CHAN1:BIAS?         /*The query returns 2.000000E-03.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the deskew (delay calibration) time of the specified channel, in seconds.
remarks: - The deskew can only be changed while the horizontal scale is 10 µs/div or faster. On a slower time base the value is not applied and error `-224,"Illegal parameter value" timebase` is generated.
- A value outside the range, or one that is not a number, generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
- `<n>` accepts 1 to 4 whatever the number of inputs of the connected model; any other value generates error `-113,"Undefined header"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the deskew time in scientific notation, for example `2.000000E-09`.
commands.example:
:CHAN2:TCAL 2e-9    /*Delays CH2 by 2 ns.*/
:CHAN2:TCAL?        /*The query returns 2.000000E-09.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the label text of the specified channel.
remarks: - Surrounding double quotes are removed. Text longer than 10 characters is truncated to the first 10.
- An empty string removes the label, which also turns label display off (`:CHANnel<n>:LABel:SHOW?` returns `0`).
- `<n>` accepts 1 to 4 whatever the number of inputs of the connected model; any other value generates error `-113,"Undefined header"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the label text without quotes, or an empty line when the channel has no label.
commands.example:
:CHAN1:LAB:CONT "CLK"    /*Sets the label of CH1 to CLK.*/
:CHAN1:LAB:CONT?         /*The query returns CLK.*/

commands.desc: Turns the label of the specified channel on or off, or queries whether a label is shown.
remarks: - A label is shown whenever its text is not empty. OFF therefore clears the label text; ON sets the text to `CH<n>` if it is empty and keeps an existing text otherwise.
- `<n>` accepts 1 to 4 whatever the number of inputs of the connected model; any other value generates error `-113,"Undefined header"`.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` if the channel has a non-empty label, otherwise `0`.
commands.example:
:CHAN1:LAB:SHOW ON    /*Shows the CH1 label (CH1 if no text was set).*/
:CHAN1:LAB:SHOW?      /*The query returns 1.*/

subsystems.title: :TIMebase Commands
subsystems.intro: The :TIMebase commands set the main horizontal scale and delay, the zoom (delayed) window, the horizontal expansion reference, roll and the XY display mode.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the main horizontal scale, in s/div.
params: 50 ps/div to 1000 s/div in a 1-2-5 sequence
remarks: - A value between steps is set to the nearest step; zero or a negative value selects 50 ps/div.
- Scales below 1 ns/div are display scales for stored records; live acquisition still samples as at 1 ns/div.
- Setting the scale resets the horizontal fine factor to 1.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-113,"Undefined header"` followed by the header.
commands.returns: The query returns the horizontal scale in scientific notation, for example `2.000000E-04`.
commands.example:
:TIM:SCAL 0.0002    /*Sets the main time base to 200 us/div.*/
:TIM:SCAL?          /*The query returns 2.000000E-04.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the horizontal delay (position of the trigger point) of the main time base, in seconds.
remarks: - The value is not limited to a range.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-113,"Undefined header"` followed by the header.
commands.returns: The query returns the delay in scientific notation, for example `1.000000E-03`.
commands.example:
:TIM:OFFS 0.001    /*Sets the horizontal delay to 1 ms.*/
:TIM:OFFS?         /*The query returns 1.000000E-03.*/

commands.desc: Turns fine adjustment of the horizontal scale on or off, or queries its state.
remarks: - Turning it OFF resets the fine factor to 1, returning the time base to a 1-2-5 step.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` or `0`.
commands.example:
:TIM:VERN ON    /*Turns fine horizontal adjustment on.*/
:TIM:VERN?      /*The query returns 1.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the horizontal expansion reference, the point the waveform expands or compresses around when the horizontal scale changes.
remarks: - CENTer: screen centre. LB (or LEFT): left border. RB (or RIGHt): right border. TRIGger: trigger position.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns `CENT`, `LB`, `RB` or `TRIG`.
commands.example:
:TIM:HREF:MODE TRIG    /*Expands around the trigger position.*/
:TIM:HREF:MODE?        /*The query returns TRIG.*/

commands.desc: Turns the zoom (delayed sweep) window on or off, or queries its state.
remarks: - An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` or `0`.
commands.example:
:TIM:DEL:ENAB ON    /*Turns the zoom window on.*/
:TIM:DEL:ENAB?      /*The query returns 1.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the horizontal scale of the zoom window, in s/div.
params: 50 ps/div up to the main scale, 1-2-5 sequence
remarks: - The value is set to the nearest step and is then limited so that it is not slower than the main time base.
- The zoom window is then kept inside the acquired record.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns the zoom scale in scientific notation, for example `1.000000E-06`.
commands.example:
:TIM:DEL:SCAL 1e-6    /*Sets the zoom scale to 1 us/div.*/
:TIM:DEL:SCAL?        /*The query returns 1.000000E-06.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the centre time of the zoom window, in seconds.
params: Any finite value; refer to Remarks
remarks: - After the value is applied the zoom window is moved, if necessary, so that it stays inside the acquired record. Query the value back to read the position actually used.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns the zoom window position in scientific notation, for example `2.000000E-05`.
commands.example:
:TIM:DEL:OFFS 2e-5    /*Centres the zoom window at 20 us.*/
:TIM:DEL:OFFS?        /*The query returns 2.000000E-05.*/

commands.desc: Turns automatic roll mode on or off, or queries its state.
remarks: - While ON, the display enters roll mode when the horizontal scale is 50 ms/div or slower.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` or `0`.
commands.example:
:TIM:ROLL OFF    /*Turns automatic roll off.*/
:TIM:ROLL?       /*The query returns 0.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the horizontal display mode.
remarks: - MAIN: normal Y-T display. XY: XY plot of CH1 against CH2 (the same switch as `:TIMebase:XY:ENABle`).
- ROLL is not a value of this command; use `:TIMebase:ROLL`. The zoom window is controlled with `:TIMebase:DELay:ENABle`.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns `MAIN` or `XY`.
commands.example:
:TIM:MODE XY    /*Selects the XY display.*/
:TIM:MODE?      /*The query returns XY.*/

commands.desc: Turns the XY display on or off, or queries its state.
remarks: - The XY display plots CH1 (X) against CH2 (Y). ON is equivalent to `:TIMebase:MODE XY`.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` or `0`.
commands.example:
:TIM:XY:ENAB ON    /*Turns the XY display on.*/
:TIM:XY:ENAB?      /*The query returns 1.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the X source of the XY display.
remarks: - The X source is fixed to CH1. Sending `CHANnel1` is accepted and has no effect; any other source generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `CHAN1`.
commands.example:
:TIM:XY:X CHAN1    /*Confirms CH1 as the X source.*/
:TIM:XY:X?         /*The query returns CHAN1.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the Y source of the XY display.
remarks: - The Y source is fixed to CH2. Sending `CHANnel2` is accepted and has no effect; any other source generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `CHAN2`.
commands.example:
:TIM:XY:Y CHAN2    /*Confirms CH2 as the Y source.*/
:TIM:XY:Y?         /*The query returns CHAN2.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the Z (intensity) source of the XY display.
remarks: - NONE or OFF removes the Z input.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns `CHAN1`, `CHAN2`, `CHAN3`, `CHAN4` or `NONE`.
commands.example:
:TIM:XY:Z CHAN3    /*Uses CH3 as the Z input of the XY display.*/
:TIM:XY:Z?         /*The query returns CHAN3.*/

subsystems.title: :TRIGger Commands
subsystems.intro: The :TRIGger commands set the trigger type, sweep mode, sources, edge level and slope, holdoff and noise rejection, and query the trigger status. A reference (R1 to R10) can be the trigger source; the acquisition then replays that stored record instead of the live inputs.

commands.desc: Selects or queries the trigger type.
remarks: - This command selects the trigger type, not the sweep; the sweep is set with `:TRIGger:SWEep`.
- The full names are also accepted: PULSE, SLOPE, VIDEO, PATTERN, DURATION, TIMEOUT, WINDOW, DELAY, SETUPHOLD (or SET), NTHEDGE (or NTH, NEDGE). Tokens are matched exactly, case-insensitively.
- An unknown type generates error `-224,"Invalid trigger type"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `EDGE`, `PULS`, `SLOP`, `VID`, `PATT`, `DUR`, `TIM`, `RUNT`, `WIND`, `DEL`, `SET`, `NEDG` or `BUS`.
commands.example:
:TRIG:MODE PULS    /*Selects the pulse trigger.*/
:TRIG:MODE?        /*The query returns PULS.*/

commands.desc: Selects or queries the trigger type. The command form is identical to `:TRIGger:MODE`; the query returns the display name of the type.
remarks: - An unknown type generates error `-224,"Invalid trigger type"`.
- Use `:TRIGger:MODE?` when a short token is required.
commands.returns: The query returns the display name: `Edge`, `Pulse`, `Slope`, `Video`, `Pattern`, `Duration`, `Timeout`, `Runt`, `Window`, `Delay`, `Setup/Hold`, `Nth edge` or `Bus`.
commands.example:
:TRIG:TYP SETUPHOLD    /*Selects the setup/hold trigger.*/
:TRIG:TYP?             /*The query returns Setup/Hold.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the trigger sweep mode.
remarks: - AUTO: the instrument acquires even when no trigger occurs. NORMal: the instrument acquires only on a trigger. SINGle: one acquisition on the next trigger, then stop.
- Any argument that begins with `AUTO`, `NORM` or `SING` is accepted.
- Selecting SINGle while the acquisition is running arms a new single acquisition that `*OPC?` waits for.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-113,"Undefined header"` followed by the command text.
commands.returns: The query returns `AUTO`, `NORM` or `SING`.
commands.example:
:TRIG:SWE NORM    /*Selects the Normal sweep.*/
:TRIG:SWE?        /*The query returns NORM.*/

commands.desc: Queries the current trigger status.
remarks: - STOP is returned whenever the acquisition is stopped, including after a Single acquisition has completed.
- The header is answered with or without the `?`.
commands.returns: The query returns `TD` (triggered), `WAIT` (waiting for a trigger), `AUTO` (acquiring without a trigger) or `STOP`.
commands.example: :TRIG:STAT?    /*The query returns TD.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the trigger holdoff time, in seconds.
remarks: - A value outside the range is not applied and generates error `-113,"Undefined header"` followed by the command text.
commands.returns: The query returns the holdoff time in scientific notation, for example `1.000000E-06`.
commands.example:
:TRIG:HOLD 1e-6    /*Sets the holdoff time to 1 us.*/
:TRIG:HOLD?        /*The query returns 1.000000E-06.*/

commands.desc: Turns trigger noise rejection on or off, or queries its state.
remarks: - An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-113,"Undefined header"` followed by the command text.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` or `0`.
commands.example:
:TRIG:NREJ ON    /*Turns noise rejection on.*/
:TRIG:NREJ?      /*The query returns 1.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the source of the edge trigger.
remarks: - This is the primary trigger source shared by all trigger types (see `:TRIGger:SOURce`).

- Selecting a reference switches the acquisition to replay that stored record; selecting a channel returns to the live inputs. The Run/Stop state is kept, and an armed Single acquisition is re-armed (`*OPC?` then waits for the new one).

- `CHANnel<n>` selects a live input of the model. `R<n>` (or `REF<n>`, n = 1 to 10) selects a loaded reference; a slot that holds no reference, or a channel the model does not have, generates error `-224,"Trigger source is unavailable"`. Any other token generates error `-224,"Invalid trigger source"`.
- `D0` to `D15` select a logic analyzer line and are accepted only when the logic analyzer is available and on; otherwise they generate error `-113,"Undefined header"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `CHAN<n>`, `R<n>`, or `D<n>` when a logic line is the source.
commands.example:
:TRIG:EDGE:SOUR CHAN2    /*Selects CH2 as the edge trigger source.*/
:TRIG:EDGE:SOUR?         /*The query returns CHAN2.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the primary trigger source. The same source is used by every trigger type, so `:TRIGger:SOURce`, `:TRIGger:SOURce1` and any type-specific form such as `:TRIGger:PULSe:SOURce` are equivalent.
params: Any trigger-type node, for example EDGE, PULSe, SLOPe, RUNT
remarks: - Selecting a reference switches the acquisition to replay that stored record; selecting a channel returns to the live inputs. The Run/Stop state is kept, and an armed Single acquisition is re-armed.

- `CHANnel<n>` selects a live input of the model. `R<n>` (or `REF<n>`, n = 1 to 10) selects a loaded reference; a slot that holds no reference, or a channel the model does not have, generates error `-224,"Trigger source is unavailable"`. Any other token generates error `-224,"Invalid trigger source"`.
- Logic analyzer lines (`D0` to `D15`) are accepted through `:TRIGger:EDGE:SOURce`.
commands.returns: The query returns `CHAN<n>`, `R<n>`, or `D<n>` when a logic line is the source.
commands.example:
:TRIG:PULS:SOUR R1    /*Triggers on the stored record in reference slot R1.*/
:TRIG:SOUR?           /*The query returns R1.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the secondary trigger source used by trigger types that compare two signals, such as Delay and Setup/Hold.
params: Any trigger-type node, for example DELay, SETup
remarks: - Unlike the primary source, the secondary source does not change which record is acquired.

- `CHANnel<n>` selects a live input of the model. `R<n>` (or `REF<n>`, n = 1 to 10) selects a loaded reference; a slot that holds no reference, or a channel the model does not have, generates error `-224,"Trigger source is unavailable"`. Any other token generates error `-224,"Invalid trigger source"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `CHAN<n>` or `R<n>`.
commands.example:
:TRIG:DEL:SOUR2 CHAN2    /*Selects CH2 as the second source of the delay trigger.*/
:TRIG:SOUR2?              /*The query returns CHAN2.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the trigger level, in volts.
remarks: - The level is shared with the upper threshold of the runt trigger (`:TRIGger:RUNT:UPPer`).
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-113,"Undefined header"` followed by the command text.
commands.returns: The query returns the trigger level in scientific notation, for example `1.500000E+00`.
commands.example:
:TRIG:EDGE:LEV 1.5    /*Sets the trigger level to 1.5 V.*/
:TRIG:EDGE:LEV?       /*The query returns 1.500000E+00.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the edge type of the edge trigger.
remarks: - POSitive: rising edge. NEGative: falling edge. RFALl: either edge.
- Any argument that begins with `POS`, `NEG` or `RFAL` is accepted.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-113,"Undefined header"` followed by the command text.
commands.returns: The query returns `POS`, `NEG` or `RFAL`.
commands.example:
:TRIG:EDGE:SLOP NEG    /*Triggers on the falling edge.*/
:TRIG:EDGE:SLOP?       /*The query returns NEG.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the upper threshold of the runt trigger, in volts.
remarks: - The upper threshold and the main trigger level (`:TRIGger:EDGE:LEVel`) are the same setting; changing one changes the other.
- A value that is not a number generates error `-224,"Invalid runt threshold"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the threshold in scientific notation, for example `2.000000E+00`.
commands.example:
:TRIG:RUNT:UPP 2    /*Sets the upper runt threshold to 2 V.*/
:TRIG:RUNT:UPP?     /*The query returns 2.000000E+00.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the lower threshold of the runt trigger, in volts.
remarks: - A value that is not a number generates error `-224,"Invalid runt threshold"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the threshold in scientific notation, for example `5.000000E-01`.
commands.example:
:TRIG:RUNT:LOW 0.5    /*Sets the lower runt threshold to 500 mV.*/
:TRIG:RUNT:LOW?       /*The query returns 5.000000E-01.*/

subsystems.title: :WAVeform Commands
subsystems.intro: The :WAVeform commands read waveform data from a channel or a reference. Select the source, mode, format and point range, read the preamble for the scaling factors, then read the data. The transfer settings are held by the remote interface: they are not part of the instrument setup, are not changed by `*RST`, and do not affect the trigger or the display. Clients connected to the same raw TCP port share them.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the source of the waveform data transfer.
remarks: - Reading a reference (`R<n>`; `REF<n>` is accepted as an alias) is an OOS extension.
- The transfer source does not select the trigger source or change the acquisition.
- A command with an empty argument is ignored; any other invalid source generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `CHAN<n>` or `R<n>`.
commands.example:
:WAV:SOUR CHAN2    /*Reads CH2 data.*/
:WAV:SOUR?         /*The query returns CHAN2.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the waveform reading mode.
remarks: - NORMal: reads the waveform displayed on the screen.
- RAW: reads the waveform in internal memory (the full record).
- MAXimum: reads the internal memory while the instrument is stopped and the screen waveform while it is running.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns `NORM`, `MAX` or `RAW`.
commands.example:
:WAV:MODE RAW    /*Reads the full record.*/
:WAV:MODE?       /*The query returns RAW.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the format of the returned waveform data.
remarks: - BYTE: one unsigned byte per point (codes 0 to 255).
- WORD: two bytes per point, unsigned 16-bit, **little-endian** (low byte first), codes 0 to 65535.
- ASCii: the voltage of each point in scientific notation, separated by commas.
- An invalid format leaves the setting unchanged and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `BYTE`, `WORD` or `ASC`.
commands.example:
:WAV:FORM WORD    /*Selects 16-bit data.*/
:WAV:FORM?        /*The query returns WORD.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the first point of the waveform data to read.
remarks: - Points are numbered from 1.
- If a stop point has been set and is smaller than `<start>`, the stop point is raised to `<start>`.
- A start point beyond the end of the data selects no points (`:WAVeform:POINts?` returns `0`).
- A value that is not an integer of 1 or greater generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the start point as an integer, for example `1`.
commands.example:
:WAV:STAR 1001    /*Starts reading at point 1001.*/
:WAV:STAR?        /*The query returns 1001.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the last point of the waveform data to read.
remarks: - The stop point is inclusive. A value beyond the end of the data reads up to the last point.
- If `<stop>` is smaller than the start point, the start point is lowered to `<stop>`.
- Until a stop point is set (with this command or `:WAVeform:POINts`), reading continues to the last point of the source.
- A value that is not an integer of 1 or greater generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the stop point as an integer. When no stop point has been set, it returns the current number of points of the source.
commands.example:
:WAV:STOP 2000    /*Stops reading at point 2000.*/
:WAV:STOP?        /*The query returns 2000.*/

commands.desc: Sets the number of points to read from the start point, or queries the number of points the next data read returns.
remarks: - Setting `<count>` sets the stop point to start point + `<count>` − 1.
- The query reports the points actually available in the selected range, limited to the data of the source; it returns `0` when the start point is beyond the end of the data.
- A value that is not an integer of 1 or greater generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the number of points as an integer, for example `1000`.
commands.example:
:WAV:POIN 1000    /*Reads 1000 points from the start point.*/
:WAV:POIN?        /*The query returns 1000.*/

commands.desc: Queries the waveform parameters of the current source, mode, format and point range.
remarks: - Convert a BYTE or WORD code to volts with: voltage = (code − yorigin − yreference) × yincrement.
- The time of point i of the page (i from 0) is: xorigin + i × xincrement.
- yincrement is (vertical scale × 8) / 250 for BYTE and ASCii and (vertical scale × 8) / 60000 for WORD.
- The preamble does not transfer any sample data.
commands.returns: The query returns 10 comma-separated fields: `<format>,<type>,<points>,<count>,<xincrement>,<xorigin>,<xreference>,<yincrement>,<yorigin>,<yreference>`. format: `0` (BYTE), `1` (WORD) or `2` (ASCii). type: `0` (NORMal), `1` (MAXimum) or `2` (RAW). points: number of points in the page (integer). count: always `1`. xincrement: sample interval in seconds, in scientific notation. xorigin: time of the first point of the page, in scientific notation. xreference: always `0`. yincrement: volts per code, in scientific notation. yorigin: vertical offset in codes, as a plain integer (for example `0` or `-48`). yreference: `128` (BYTE, ASCii) or `32768` (WORD).

commands.desc: Reads the waveform data of the current source between the start and stop points.
remarks: - The data is returned as an IEEE 488.2 definite-length block: `#9`, nine digits giving the number of data bytes, then the data.
- BYTE: one byte per point. WORD: two bytes per point, little-endian. Codes outside the range of the format are clipped to its limits (0/255 or 0/65535).
- ASCii: comma-separated voltages in scientific notation inside the block.

- If the selected range would exceed the 64 MiB reply limit, no data is returned and error `-223,"Too much data; select a shorter waveform page"` is generated. Read long records in several pages with `:WAVeform:STARt` and `:WAVeform:STOP`.
commands.returns: The query returns a definite-length block, for example `#9000001000` followed by 1000 data bytes in BYTE format.
commands.example:
:WAV:SOUR CHAN1    /*Selects CH1.*/
:WAV:FORM BYTE     /*Selects byte data.*/
:WAV:DATA?         /*The query returns #9000001000 followed by 1000 bytes.*/

subsystems.title: :DISPlay Commands
subsystems.intro: The :DISPlay commands set the waveform drawing, persistence, brightness, graticule and color grading, and capture the screen image.

commands.desc: Reads the current screen image.
remarks: - Without a parameter a 24-bit BMP image is returned.
- An unknown format generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the image as an IEEE 488.2 definite-length block: `#9`, nine digits giving the number of bytes, then the BMP or PNG file data.
commands.example: :DISP:DATA? PNG    /*The query returns #9 followed by nine length digits and the PNG file.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries how the waveform is drawn.
remarks: - VECTors: adjacent sample points are joined with lines. DOTS: only the sample points are drawn.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns `VECT` or `DOTS`.
commands.example:
:DISP:TYPE VECT    /*Draws the waveform as vectors.*/
:DISP:TYPE?        /*The query returns VECT.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the persistence time of the display.
remarks: - A number of seconds of 0 or greater is accepted and set to the nearest listed time; `0` selects MIN. Large values select 10, not INFinite.
- MIN: minimum persistence. INFinite: points stay until the display is cleared (`:CLEar`).
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns `MIN`, `0.1`, `0.5`, `1`, `5`, `10` or `INF`.
commands.example:
:DISP:GRAD:TIME 1    /*Sets the persistence time to 1 s.*/
:DISP:GRAD:TIME?     /*The query returns 1.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the waveform brightness, in percent.
remarks: - Values from 1 to 9 are accepted and set to 10, the lowest brightness used.
- A value outside 1 to 100, or one that is not an integer, generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the brightness as an integer, for example `60`.
commands.example:
:DISP:WBR 60    /*Sets the waveform brightness to 60%.*/
:DISP:WBR?      /*The query returns 60.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the graticule brightness, in percent.
remarks: - Values from 0 to 9 are accepted and set to 10, the lowest brightness used.
- A value outside 0 to 100, or one that is not an integer, generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the brightness as an integer, for example `50`.
commands.example:
:DISP:GBR 50    /*Sets the graticule brightness to 50%.*/
:DISP:GBR?      /*The query returns 50.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the graticule type.
remarks: - FULL: full grid. HALF: light grid. NONE: no grid.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns `FULL`, `HALF` or `NONE`.
commands.example:
:DISP:GRID HALF    /*Selects the light grid.*/
:DISP:GRID?        /*The query returns HALF.*/

commands.desc: Turns the graticule rulers on or off, or queries their state.
remarks: - An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` or `0`.
commands.example:
:DISP:RUL OFF    /*Hides the rulers.*/
:DISP:RUL?       /*The query returns 0.*/

commands.desc: Turns color grading of the waveform on or off, or queries its state.
remarks: - With color grading on, the color of each point shows how often it is hit.
- An invalid value is not applied and generates error `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` followed by the argument.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` or `0`.
commands.example:
:DISP:COL ON    /*Turns color grading on.*/
:DISP:COL?      /*The query returns 1.*/

subsystems.title: :MEASure Commands
subsystems.intro: The :MEASure commands add measurement items to the readout, query measurement results and statistics, and set the measurement thresholds, sources and range. Standard items are listed in Appendix A and pair items in Appendix B.

commands.desc: Adds the specified measurement item to the measurement readout, or queries the measurement result of the specified item. Standard items take one source; pair items (delay, phase, skew, setup and hold) take source A and source B. The query computes the value directly and does not require the item to be on the readout.
params: Standard items: refer to Appendix A. Pair items: refer to Appendix B.
`CHAN<n>` (n = 1 to 4) or `R<n>` (n = 1 to 10); `REF<n>` is accepted as an alias
`CHAN<n>` (n = 1 to 4) or `R<n>` (n = 1 to 10); `REF<n>` is accepted as an alias; pair items only
remarks: - Item names are accepted in long or short form, case-insensitively (for example `FREQuency` or `FREQ`).
- Set form: adding an item that is already on the readout with the same sources keeps the existing row and its statistics; no second row is created.

- Set form: when the readout already holds the maximum number of rows (1024 in total for standard, pair and catalogue rows), a standard item raises `-223,"Measurement selection is full"`; a pair item raises `-224,"Measurement selection is full"`.
- Set form: a pair item whose source A and source B are the same raises `-224,"Source A and B are the same source"`. More sources than the item takes raise `-224,"Too many measurement sources"`.

- Query form: a standard item without a source uses the :MEASure:SOURce A selection. A pair item query requires both <srcA> and <srcB>; if <srcB> is missing, `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` is raised and `9.9E37` is returned.

- Query form: `SETHold` (alias `SHOLD`, query only) accepts either no sources (the Measure A and B selections are used) or exactly two sources (clock, data); any other count raises `-224` and returns `9.9E37`.

- For SETUP/HOLD/SETHOLD, FSETUP/FHOLD and DSETUP/DHOLD/DSETHOLD, source A is the clock (strobe) and source B is the data. SETUP/HOLD latch on rising clock edges, FSETUP/FHOLD on falling edges and the `D` items on both strobe edges, as a DDR DQS strobe does. A clock edge counts only when the data changed within that edge's own cycle; data that holds steady between strobe bursts adds no setup or hold result.
- SETHOLD and DSETHOLD return the number of latching edges that violate the :MEASure:TSETup or :MEASure:THOLd limit.
- An unknown item, or a source token that is not `CHAN<n>`/`R<n>`/`REF<n>`, raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`; the query then returns `9.9E37`.
- The measured span is controlled by :MEASure:GATing.
- `9.9E37` is returned when no valid value exists (no data, the result is unavailable, or it is still being calculated).
commands.returns: The query returns the measurement value in scientific notation in base units (V, s, Hz, %, degrees, V*s, V/s, or a count), for example `1.966000E-10`.
commands.example:
:MEAS:ITEM VPP,CHAN1    /*Adds Vpp of CH1 to the measurement readout.*/
:MEAS:ITEM? VPP,CHAN1    /*The query returns 3.300000E+00.*/
:MEAS:ITEM? RRDELAY,CHAN1,CHAN2    /*The query returns 2.500000E-09.*/
:MEAS:ITEM? DSETUP,CHAN1,CHAN2    /*CH1 = DQS strobe, CH2 = DQ data, both strobe edges. The query returns 1.966000E-10.*/
:MEAS:ITEM? DHOLD,CHAN1,CHAN2    /*The query returns 2.140000E-10.*/
:MEAS:ITEM? DSETHOLD,CHAN1,CHAN2    /*Number of strobe edges violating TSETup/THOLd. The query returns 0.000000E+00.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the default measurement source. The optional second source sets the default source B used by pair items.
params: `CHAN<n>` (n = 1 to 4) or `R<n>` (n = 1 to 10); `REF<n>` is accepted as an alias
`CHAN<n>` (n = 1 to 4) or `R<n>` (n = 1 to 10); `REF<n>` is accepted as an alias
remarks: - Source A is the same setting as :MEASure:SETup:PSA (:MEASure:SETup:DSA); source B is the same setting as :MEASure:SETup:PSB (:MEASure:SETup:DSB).
- An empty argument, more than two sources, or an invalid source raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` and nothing is changed.
commands.returns: The query returns source A only, as `CHAN<n>` or `R<n>`.
commands.example:
:MEAS:SOUR CHAN1,CHAN2    /*Sets source A to CH1 and source B to CH2.*/
:MEAS:SOUR?    /*The query returns CHAN1.*/

commands.desc: Removes all measurement items from the readout.
remarks: - Standard, pair and catalogue rows are all removed, together with their per-row settings.
- DVM and counter rows on the readout are controlled by :DVM:ENABle and :COUNter:ENABle and are not affected.
commands.example: :MEAS:CLE    /*Removes all measurement items.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the measurement range. `SCReen` measures only the part of the record visible in the current view; `NONE` measures the full record.
remarks: - An invalid argument raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `SCREEN` or `NONE`.
commands.example:
:MEAS:GAT NONE    /*Measures over the full record.*/
:MEAS:GAT?    /*The query returns NONE.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the low/high edge threshold pair, in percent of the waveform amplitude, used by edge measurements such as rise and fall time.
remarks: - Spaces in the argument are ignored. `10/90`, `1090` and `10` set 10 % and 90 %; `20/80`, `2080` and `20` set 20 % and 80 %.

- This command sets the same thresholds as :MEASure:SETup:MIN and :MEASure:SETup:MAX. The query returns `10/90` when the low threshold is below 15 % and the high threshold above 85 %; any other combination is reported as `20/80`.
- The last record is re-measured with the new thresholds.
commands.returns: The query returns `10/90` or `20/80`.
commands.example:
:MEAS:REFS 20/80    /*Sets the thresholds to 20 % and 80 %.*/
:MEAS:REFS?    /*The query returns 20/80.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the upper threshold of the measurement, in percent of the waveform amplitude.
params: 0 to 100; must be greater than the lower threshold
remarks: - A value outside 0 to 100 raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`. A value not greater than the current lower threshold raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value" below the lower threshold`.
- The last record is re-measured with the new threshold.
commands.returns: The query returns the threshold as an integer percent, rounded, for example `90`.
commands.example:
:MEAS:SET:MAX 80    /*Sets the upper threshold to 80 %.*/
:MEAS:SET:MAX?    /*The query returns 80.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the lower threshold of the measurement, in percent of the waveform amplitude.
params: 0 to 100; must be less than the upper threshold
remarks: - A value outside 0 to 100 raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`. A value not less than the current upper threshold raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value" above the upper threshold`.
- The last record is re-measured with the new threshold.
commands.returns: The query returns the threshold as an integer percent, rounded, for example `10`.
commands.example:
:MEAS:SET:MIN 20    /*Sets the lower threshold to 20 %.*/
:MEAS:SET:MIN?    /*The query returns 20.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries source A of the phase and delay measurements.
params: `CHAN<n>` (n = 1 to 4) or `R<n>` (n = 1 to 10); `REF<n>` is accepted as an alias
remarks: - Source A is the same setting as the source set by :MEASure:SOURce; changing one changes the other.
- An invalid source raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `CHAN<n>` or `R<n>`.
commands.example:
:MEAS:SET:PSA CHAN1    /*Sets source A to CH1.*/
:MEAS:SET:PSA?    /*The query returns CHAN1.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries source B of the phase and delay measurements.
params: `CHAN<n>` (n = 1 to 4) or `R<n>` (n = 1 to 10); `REF<n>` is accepted as an alias
remarks: - Source B is used by pair items added or queried without an explicit second source (for example by :MEASure:ITEM and by the SETHold query without sources).
- An invalid source raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `CHAN<n>` or `R<n>`.
commands.example:
:MEAS:SET:PSB CHAN2    /*Sets source B to CH2.*/
:MEAS:SET:PSB?    /*The query returns CHAN2.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the setup-time limit, in seconds, used by the SETHOLD and DSETHOLD violation counts.
remarks: - A negative or non-numeric value raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the limit in scientific notation, for example `2.000000E-10`.
commands.example:
:MEAS:TSET 2E-10    /*Sets the setup limit to 200 ps.*/
:MEAS:TSET?    /*The query returns 2.000000E-10.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the hold-time limit, in seconds, used by the SETHOLD and DSETHOLD violation counts.
remarks: - A negative or non-numeric value raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the limit in scientific notation, for example `1.500000E-10`.
commands.example:
:MEAS:THOL 1.5E-10    /*Sets the hold limit to 150 ps.*/
:MEAS:THOL?    /*The query returns 1.500000E-10.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the burst idle interval, in seconds, used to separate bursts for the burst width (BWIDth) measurement.
remarks: - The last record is re-measured with the new interval.
- A negative or non-numeric value raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the interval in scientific notation, for example `1.000000E-06`.
commands.example:
:MEAS:BURS:IDLE 1E-6    /*Sets the idle interval to 1 us.*/
:MEAS:BURS:IDLE?    /*The query returns 1.000000E-06.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries which side of the threshold levels is counted by the time-outside (TOUTside) measurement.
remarks: - The last record is re-measured with the new setting.
- An invalid argument raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `ABOV`, `BEL` or `BOTH`.
commands.example:
:MEAS:OUTS ABOV    /*Counts time above the upper level only.*/
:MEAS:OUTS?    /*The query returns ABOV.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the number of edge intervals spanned by the duration-of-N-periods (NPERiods) measurement.
remarks: - The last record is re-measured with the new setting.
- A value outside 1 to 32 raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns an integer, for example `4`.
commands.example:
:MEAS:NPER 4    /*Measures the duration of 4 periods.*/
:MEAS:NPER?    /*The query returns 4.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the edges used by the duration-of-N-periods (NPERiods) measurement. `CLOCk` uses rising mid-level crossings only; `DATA` uses mid-level crossings in either direction.
remarks: - The last record is re-measured with the new setting.
- An invalid argument raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `CLOC` or `DATA`.
commands.example:
:MEAS:EDG DATA    /*Uses both edge directions.*/
:MEAS:EDG?    /*The query returns DATA.*/

commands.desc: Turns on or off the measurement indicators (labels drawn on the trace), or queries their status.
remarks: - :CURSor:MEASure:INDicator controls the same setting.
- An invalid argument raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` or `0`.
commands.example:
:MEAS:IND ON    /*Turns on the measurement indicators.*/
:MEAS:IND?    /*The query returns 1.*/

commands.desc: Queries every row of the measurement readout and its current value in one reply.
remarks: - Rows are listed in this order: standard rows, pair rows, catalogue rows, then the DVM row (only while :DVM:ENABle is ON) and the counter row (only while :COUNter:ENABle is ON).
- The item token is the canonical upper-case long form (for example `FREQUENCY`, `RRDELAY`); refer to Appendix A and Appendix B.
- Catalogue rows (analysis items selected on the measurement catalogue, Appendix D) cannot be queried individually with :MEASure:ITEM?; read them here.
- When the readout is empty, the reply is an empty line.
- `9.9E37` is returned when no valid value exists (no data, the result is unavailable, or it is still being calculated).
commands.returns:
The query returns the rows separated by `;`. Row formats:
Standard: `<ITEM>,<src>,<value>`
Pair: `<ITEM>,<srcA>,<srcB>,<value>`
Catalogue: `CAT<id>,<srcA>,<srcB>,<srcC>,<srcD>,<value>` (unused source roles are still listed)
DVM: `DVM,<DC|ACRMS|ACDC>,CHAN<n>,<value>`
Counter: `COUNTER,<FREQUENCY|PERIOD|TOTALIZE>,CHAN<n>,<value>`
Sources are `CHAN<n>` or `R<n>`; values are in scientific notation.
commands.example: :MEAS:STR?    /*The query returns VPP,CHAN1,3.300000E+00;FREQUENCY,CHAN1,1.000000E+06;RRDELAY,CHAN1,CHAN2,2.500000E-09;DVM,DC,CHAN1,1.650000E+00.*/

commands.desc: Queries every measurement shown on the screen: the measurement readout rows and, while the Eye page is displayed, every Eye figure.
remarks: - The Eye figures are appended only while :VIEW? returns `EYE`; refer to Appendix C for the figure names.
- When nothing is shown, the reply is an empty line.
- `9.9E37` is returned when no valid value exists (no data, the result is unavailable, or it is still being calculated).
commands.returns: The query returns the :MEASure:STRip? rows followed by one `<FIGURE>,<value>` row per Eye figure (figure name in upper-case long form, for example `HEIGHT`), all separated by `;`. Values are in scientific notation.
commands.example: :MEAS:READ?    /*With the Eye page displayed, the query returns VPP,CHAN1,3.300000E+00;ONE,1.200000E+00;ZERO,1.000000E-01;...;NPJ,9.9E37.*/

commands.desc: Turns on or off the statistics display of the measurement readout, or queries its status.
remarks: - Hiding the statistics keeps the accumulated observations; they are shown again when the display is turned back on.
- An invalid argument raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` or `0`.
commands.example:
:MEAS:STAT:DISP ON    /*Shows the measurement statistics.*/
:MEAS:STAT:DISP?    /*The query returns 1.*/

commands.desc: Clears the statistics history of all measurement rows.
remarks: - The rows themselves stay on the readout. No new acquisition is started.
commands.example: :MEAS:STAT:RES    /*Clears the measurement statistics.*/

commands.desc: Adds the specified measurement item to the readout and turns on the statistics display, or queries one statistic of the specified item.
params: Standard items: refer to Appendix A. Pair items: refer to Appendix B.
`CHAN<n>` (n = 1 to 4) or `R<n>` (n = 1 to 10); `REF<n>` is accepted as an alias
`CHAN<n>` (n = 1 to 4) or `R<n>` (n = 1 to 10); `REF<n>` is accepted as an alias; pair items only
remarks: - Set form: behaves as :MEASure:ITEM (same errors); the statistics display is turned on only if no error was raised.
- Query form: `CNT` and `COUNt` return the number of observations. A row that is not on the readout has a count of 0 and `9.9E37` for the other statistics.
- `DEViation` (standard deviation) needs more than one observation; otherwise `9.9E37` is returned.
- The current value uses the row's own settings on the readout where applicable.
- An invalid <type>, item or source raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` and returns `9.9E37`. An unknown node below :MEASure:STATistic raises `-113,"Undefined header"`.
- `9.9E37` is returned when no valid value exists (no data, the result is unavailable, or it is still being calculated).
commands.returns: The query returns the statistic in scientific notation; the count is also returned in scientific notation, for example `1.200000E+01`.
commands.example:
:MEAS:STAT:ITEM VPP,CHAN1    /*Adds Vpp of CH1 and shows statistics.*/
:MEAS:STAT:ITEM? MAX,VPP,CHAN1    /*The query returns 3.312000E+00.*/
:MEAS:STAT:ITEM? CNT,VPP,CHAN1    /*The query returns 1.200000E+01.*/

subsystems.title: :EYE Commands
subsystems.intro: The :EYE command queries the figures of the Eye diagram analysis. The Eye figures are listed in Appendix C.

commands.desc: Queries one figure of the current Eye diagram result, such as eye height, eye width, unit interval or total jitter.
remarks: - Figure names are accepted in long or short form, case-insensitively. Any text after a comma is ignored.
- The query reads the result of the Eye analysis as currently configured; it does not run the one-click Auto Eye.

- A full-record Eye of a long reference is calculated in the background. Until it finishes, the previous result is returned; check that `EDGES` and `UI` belong to the new source before reading the other figures.
- With an Eye clock source such as a DDR DQS strobe, the data is folded on each strobe edge, so bursts that start at unrelated phases line up as the receiver latches them.
- An unknown figure raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"` and returns `9.9E37`.
- `9.9E37` is returned when no valid value exists (no data, the result is unavailable, or it is still being calculated).
commands.returns: The query returns the figure in scientific notation, for example `3.125000E-10`.
commands.example:
:VIEW EYE    /*Displays the Eye page.*/
:EYE:ITEM? WIDTH    /*The query returns 2.410000E-10.*/

subsystems.title: Analysis Page Commands
subsystems.intro: These commands query results of the analysis pages (:POWer, :SPECtrum, :MAGnetic, :INVerter, :DPT, :BANDwidth), control the Bode sweep (:BODE) and select the displayed page (:VIEW). They are OOS extensions. The analysis items are listed in Appendix D.

commands.desc: Queries one power analysis result, such as real power, power factor, switching loss or ripple.
params: `CHAN<n>` (n = 1 to 4) or `R<n>` (n = 1 to 10); `REF<n>` is accepted as an alias
remarks: - Item names are matched case-insensitively and must be given in full (no short forms).
- The number of sources depends on the item (refer to Appendix D): most items take none or two (voltage, current); ripple and inrush items take none or one; rail items take up to three.
- When sources are omitted, the sources configured on the analysis page are used. The analysis page does not need to be displayed.
- An invalid source token, an unknown item or a wrong number of sources raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`; the query then returns `9.9E37`.
- `9.9E37` is returned when no valid value exists (no data, the result is unavailable, or it is still being calculated).
commands.returns: The query returns the result in scientific notation, for example `1.250000E+01`.
commands.example: :POW:ITEM? REAL,CHAN1,CHAN2    /*Real power with V on CH1 and I on CH2. The query returns 1.250000E+01.*/

commands.desc: Queries the current harmonics of the specified source, up to the 40th order.
params: `CHAN<n>` (n = 1 to 4) or `R<n>` (n = 1 to 10); `REF<n>` is accepted as an alias
The current source of the Power page
remarks: - When the source is omitted, the current source configured on the Power page is used.
- `9.9E37` is returned when no harmonics can be calculated.
- An invalid source token, an unknown item or a wrong number of sources raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`; the query then returns `9.9E37`.
commands.returns: The query returns `<order>,<amplitude>` pairs separated by `;`; the order is an integer and the rms amplitude (A) is in scientific notation.

commands.desc: Queries one spectrum analysis result, such as THD, SNR, SFDR, ENOB or ACPR.
params: `CHAN<n>` (n = 1 to 4) or `R<n>` (n = 1 to 10); `REF<n>` is accepted as an alias
remarks: - Item names are matched case-insensitively and must be given in full.
- When the distortion analysis cannot run on the source data, `9.9E37` is returned without an error, even for an unknown item.
- When sources are omitted, the sources configured on the analysis page are used. The analysis page does not need to be displayed.
- An invalid source token, an unknown item or a wrong number of sources raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`; the query then returns `9.9E37`.
- `9.9E37` is returned when no valid value exists (no data, the result is unavailable, or it is still being calculated).
commands.returns: The query returns the result in scientific notation, for example `-6.523000E+01`.
commands.example: :SPEC:ITEM? THD,CHAN1    /*The query returns -6.523000E+01.*/

commands.desc: Queries one magnetic analysis result: inductance, peak flux density, peak field strength, relative permeability or core loss.
params: `CHAN<n>` (n = 1 to 4) or `R<n>` (n = 1 to 10); `REF<n>` is accepted as an alias
`CHAN<n>` (n = 1 to 4) or `R<n>` (n = 1 to 10); `REF<n>` is accepted as an alias
remarks: - Either no sources or exactly two (voltage, current) are accepted.
- Results that depend on the core geometry (turns, effective area, effective length) return `9.9E37` until that geometry is configured on the Magnetic page.
- When sources are omitted, the sources configured on the analysis page are used. The analysis page does not need to be displayed.
- An invalid source token, an unknown item or a wrong number of sources raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`; the query then returns `9.9E37`.
- `9.9E37` is returned when no valid value exists (no data, the result is unavailable, or it is still being calculated).
commands.returns: The query returns the result in scientific notation, for example `4.700000E-05`.
commands.example: :MAG:ITEM? L,CHAN1,CHAN2    /*The query returns 4.700000E-05.*/

commands.desc: Queries one inverter/motor analysis result, such as d/q components, electrical frequency, speed, torque, power or efficiency.
params: `CHAN<n>` (n = 1 to 4) or `R<n>` (n = 1 to 10); `REF<n>` is accepted as an alias
remarks: - Accepted source counts: none; one (the analog angle input, only when the angle mode is Analog); three (phases A, B, C); or four (A, B, C, angle).
- Sources are refused when the angle mode is Quadrature or Hall.
- `DIR` returns a word instead of a number.
- When sources are omitted, the sources configured on the analysis page are used. The analysis page does not need to be displayed.
- An invalid source token, an unknown item or a wrong number of sources raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`; the query then returns `9.9E37`.
- `9.9E37` is returned when no valid value exists (no data, the result is unavailable, or it is still being calculated).
commands.returns: The query returns the result in scientific notation, for example `1.500000E+03`. For `DIR` the query returns `FORWARD`, `REVERSE` or `STOPPED`.
commands.example:
:INV:ITEM? SPEED    /*The query returns 1.500000E+03.*/
:INV:ITEM? DIR    /*The query returns FORWARD.*/

commands.desc: Queries one double-pulse test result, such as turn-on/turn-off energy, switching times, dv/dt, di/dt or reverse recovery.
params: `CHAN<n>` (n = 1 to 4) or `R<n>` (n = 1 to 10); `REF<n>` is accepted as an alias
`CHAN<n>` (n = 1 to 4) or `R<n>` (n = 1 to 10); `REF<n>` is accepted as an alias
`CHAN<n>` (n = 1 to 4) or `R<n>` (n = 1 to 10); `REF<n>` is accepted as an alias; gate source
remarks: - Either no sources, two (voltage, current) or three (voltage, current, gate) are accepted.
- When sources are omitted, the sources configured on the analysis page are used. The analysis page does not need to be displayed.
- An invalid source token, an unknown item or a wrong number of sources raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`; the query then returns `9.9E37`.
- `9.9E37` is returned when no valid value exists (no data, the result is unavailable, or it is still being calculated).
commands.returns: The query returns the result in scientific notation, for example `2.350000E-04`.
commands.example: :DPT:ITEM? EON,CHAN1,CHAN2,CHAN3    /*The query returns 2.350000E-04.*/

commands.desc: Queries one step-response bandwidth estimate: rise time, bandwidth derived from the rise time, or overshoot.
params: `CHAN<n>` (n = 1 to 4) or `R<n>` (n = 1 to 10); `REF<n>` is accepted as an alias
remarks: - The source must contain at least 1000 samples; otherwise `9.9E37` is returned.
- When sources are omitted, the sources configured on the analysis page are used. The analysis page does not need to be displayed.
- An invalid source token, an unknown item or a wrong number of sources raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`; the query then returns `9.9E37`.
- `9.9E37` is returned when no valid value exists (no data, the result is unavailable, or it is still being calculated).
commands.returns: The query returns the result in scientific notation, for example `3.500000E+08`.
commands.example: :BAND:ITEM? BW,CHAN1    /*The query returns 3.500000E+08.*/

commands.desc: Starts or stops the Bode (frequency response) sweep.
remarks: - A missing or invalid argument is treated as ON.
- The sweep state changes only when it differs from the requested state.
- The sweep drives the signal generator configured with :BODE:GENerator and controls the acquisition.
commands.example: :BODE:RUN ON    /*Starts the Bode sweep.*/

commands.desc: Queries the points of the Bode sweep.
remarks: - In `LOOP` and `PSRR` modes the gain is in dB; in `IMPedance` mode it is the linear Vout/Vin ratio.
- The frequency is printed with 6 significant digits and no trailing zeros (for example `1000`, `1258.93`). The gain has 3 decimals and the phase (degrees, -180 to 180) 2 decimals.
- A phase that could not be determined is printed as `NaN`.
- When the sweep has no points, the reply is an empty line.
commands.returns: The query returns the points separated by `;`, each as `<freq>,<gain>,<phase>` in fixed-point notation.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the Bode measurement mode: control-loop response, power-supply rejection ratio or impedance.
remarks: - An invalid argument raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `LOOP`, `PSRR` or `IMP`.
commands.example:
:BODE:MODE PSRR    /*Selects PSRR mode.*/
:BODE:MODE?    /*The query returns PSRR.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the network address (`ip:port`) of the signal generator driven by the Bode sweep.
params: `ip:port`, one word; enclosing quotes are removed
remarks: - An address containing whitespace raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the address without quotes, for example `192.168.1.100:5555`.
commands.example:
:BODE:GEN "192.168.1.50:5555"    /*Sets the generator address.*/
:BODE:GEN?    /*The query returns 192.168.1.50:5555.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the page shown in the main window: the oscilloscope or one of the analysis pages.
remarks: - The query returns `STEP` while the bandwidth-test page is displayed; that page cannot be selected with this command.
- :MEASure:READout? includes the Eye figures only while the view is `EYE`.
- An invalid argument raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `SCOPE`, `SPECTRUM`, `EYE`, `POWER`, `BODE`, `STEP`, `MAGNETIC`, `INVERTER` or `DPT`.
commands.example:
:VIEW EYE    /*Displays the Eye page.*/
:VIEW?    /*The query returns EYE.*/

subsystems.title: :CURSor Commands
subsystems.intro: The :CURSor commands set the cursor mode, sources and positions and query the cursor values. In the headers below, `<type>` stands for `MANual`, `TRACk` or `XY`.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the cursor mode.
remarks: - `MANual` keeps the current manual cursor type: amplitude cursors stay amplitude cursors, otherwise time cursors are used.
- An invalid argument raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`. :CURSor without a node raises `-113,"Undefined header"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `OFF`, `MAN`, `TRAC` or `XY`.
commands.example:
:CURS:MODE MAN    /*Selects manual cursors.*/
:CURS:MODE?    /*The query returns MAN.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the type of the manual cursors: time (X) or amplitude (Y).
remarks: - Setting the type also selects manual mode, except in XY mode, where the command is accepted but has no effect.
- An invalid argument raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `AMPL` while amplitude cursors are active, otherwise `TIME`.
commands.example:
:CURS:MAN:TYPE AMPL    /*Selects amplitude cursors.*/
:CURS:MAN:TYPE?    /*The query returns AMPL.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the source of cursor A (manual mode: the source of both cursors).
params: `CHAN<n>` (n = 1 to 4) or `R<n>` (n = 1 to 10); `REF<n>` is accepted as an alias; the channel must exist on the model and the reference must be loaded
remarks: - Selecting a cursor source does not change the acquisition.
- A token that is not a valid source raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`; a channel not present on the model or an empty reference raises `-224,"Cursor source is unavailable or unsupported"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `CHAN<n>` or `R<n>`.
commands.example:
:CURS:TRAC:SOUR CHAN1    /*Sets the cursor A source to CH1.*/
:CURS:TRAC:SOUR?    /*The query returns CHAN1.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the source of track cursor B, independently of cursor A.
params: `CHAN<n>` (n = 1 to 4) or `R<n>` (n = 1 to 10); `REF<n>` is accepted as an alias
remarks: - Until a B source is set, cursor B follows the cursor A source.

- Manual cursors share one source: :CURSor:MANual:SOURce2 is accepted only when it names the current cursor A source (no change), otherwise it raises `-224,"Cursor source is unavailable or unsupported"`; its query returns the cursor A source.
- A token that is not a valid source raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `CHAN<n>` or `R<n>`.
commands.example:
:CURS:TRAC:SOUR2 CHAN2    /*Sets the track cursor B source to CH2.*/
:CURS:TRAC:SOUR2?    /*The query returns CHAN2.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the time (s) position of cursor A.
params: Finite time (s), limited to the visible span
remarks: - The time is converted to a screen position and limited to the visible time span.
- Setting a time while the cursors are OFF selects manual time cursors; while amplitude cursors are active, the cursors become XY cursors and the voltage positions are kept.
- The <type> node selects the command path only; it does not change the cursor mode.
- A non-numeric or non-finite value raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the position in scientific notation, for example `-2.000000E-06`; `9.9E37` when no time cursor is placed.
commands.example:
:CURS:MAN:CAX -2E-6    /*Places cursor A.*/
:CURS:MAN:CAX?    /*The query returns -2.000000E-06.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the time (s) position of cursor B.
params: Finite time (s), limited to the visible span
remarks: - The time is converted to a screen position and limited to the visible time span.
- Setting a time while the cursors are OFF selects manual time cursors; while amplitude cursors are active, the cursors become XY cursors and the voltage positions are kept.
- The <type> node selects the command path only; it does not change the cursor mode.
- A non-numeric or non-finite value raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the position in scientific notation, for example `3.000000E-06`; `9.9E37` when no time cursor is placed.
commands.example:
:CURS:MAN:CBX 3E-6    /*Places cursor B.*/
:CURS:MAN:CBX?    /*The query returns 3.000000E-06.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the voltage (V) position of cursor A.
params: Finite voltage (V), limited to the displayed range
remarks: - The voltage is limited to the displayed range of the cursor source, including display zoom.
- Setting a voltage while the cursors are OFF selects manual amplitude cursors; while time or track cursors are active, the cursors become XY cursors and the time positions are kept.
- The query returns `9.9E37` in OFF, time and track modes.
- The <type> node selects the command path only; it does not change the cursor mode.
- A non-numeric or non-finite value raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the position in scientific notation, for example `1.200000E+00`; `9.9E37` when no voltage cursor is placed.
commands.example:
:CURS:MAN:CAY 1.2    /*Places cursor A.*/
:CURS:MAN:CAY?    /*The query returns 1.200000E+00.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the voltage (V) position of cursor B.
params: Finite voltage (V), limited to the displayed range
remarks: - The voltage is limited to the displayed range of the cursor source, including display zoom.
- Setting a voltage while the cursors are OFF selects manual amplitude cursors; while time or track cursors are active, the cursors become XY cursors and the time positions are kept.
- The query returns `9.9E37` in OFF, time and track modes.
- The <type> node selects the command path only; it does not change the cursor mode.
- A non-numeric or non-finite value raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the position in scientific notation, for example `-4.000000E-01`; `9.9E37` when no voltage cursor is placed.
commands.example:
:CURS:MAN:CBY -0.4    /*Places cursor B.*/
:CURS:MAN:CBY?    /*The query returns -4.000000E-01.*/

commands.desc: Queries the time value of cursor A.
remarks: - `9.9E37` is returned when the cursors are OFF or amplitude cursors are active.
- This command is query only; the set form raises `-113,"Undefined header"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the value in scientific notation, or `9.9E37` when it is not available.
commands.example: :CURS:MAN:AXV?    /*The query returns -2.000000E-06.*/

commands.desc: Queries the time value of cursor B.
remarks: - `9.9E37` is returned when the cursors are OFF or amplitude cursors are active.
- This command is query only; the set form raises `-113,"Undefined header"`.
