commands.returns: The query returns the value in scientific notation, or `9.9E37` when it is not available.
commands.example: :CURS:MAN:BXV?    /*The query returns 3.000000E-06.*/

commands.desc: Queries the Y value of cursor A.
remarks: - In XY and amplitude modes, the cursor's voltage position is returned. In time and track modes, the waveform value of the cursor source at the cursor A time is returned. When the cursors are OFF, `9.9E37` is returned.
- This command is query only; the set form raises `-113,"Undefined header"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the value in scientific notation, or `9.9E37` when it is not available.
commands.example: :CURS:TRAC:AYV?    /*The query returns 1.648000E+00.*/

commands.desc: Queries the Y value of cursor B.
remarks: - As :CURSor:<type>:AYValue? for cursor B. In track mode the waveform value is taken from the cursor B source (:CURSor:TRACk:SOURce2).
- This command is query only; the set form raises `-113,"Undefined header"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the value in scientific notation, or `9.9E37` when it is not available.
commands.example: :CURS:TRAC:BYV?    /*The query returns 3.200000E-02.*/

commands.desc: Queries the time difference between cursor B and cursor A (tB - tA).
remarks: - Available in time, track and XY modes; otherwise `9.9E37` is returned.
- This command is query only; the set form raises `-113,"Undefined header"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the value in scientific notation, or `9.9E37` when it is not available.
commands.example: :CURS:MAN:XDEL?    /*The query returns 5.000000E-06.*/

commands.desc: Queries the reciprocal of the absolute time difference between the cursors, 1/|tB - tA|.
remarks: - Available in time, track and XY modes when the difference is not zero; otherwise `9.9E37` is returned.
- This command is query only; the set form raises `-113,"Undefined header"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the value in scientific notation, or `9.9E37` when it is not available.
commands.example: :CURS:MAN:IXD?    /*The query returns 2.000000E+05.*/

commands.desc: Queries the Y difference between cursor B and cursor A (yB - yA).
remarks: - In track mode, `9.9E37` is returned when the A and B sources have different units.
- `9.9E37` is returned when either Y value is unavailable.
- This command is query only; the set form raises `-113,"Undefined header"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the value in scientific notation, or `9.9E37` when it is not available.
commands.example: :CURS:TRAC:YDEL?    /*The query returns -1.616000E+00.*/

subsystems.title: :DVM Commands
subsystems.intro: The :DVM commands control the digital voltmeter and query its reading.

commands.desc: Turns on or off the digital voltmeter, or queries its status.
remarks: - While the DVM is on, its reading is also listed by :MEASure:STRip?.
- An invalid argument raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` or `0`.
commands.example:
:DVM:ENAB ON    /*Turns on the DVM.*/
:DVM:ENAB?    /*The query returns 1.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the source of the digital voltmeter.
remarks: - Only analog channels are accepted; references are not.
- An invalid argument raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `CHAN<n>`.
commands.example:
:DVM:SOUR CHAN2    /*Sets the DVM source to CH2.*/
:DVM:SOUR?    /*The query returns CHAN2.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the mode of the digital voltmeter: `DC` (average), `ACRMs` (AC rms) or `ACDCrms` (rms including DC).
remarks: - `ACRMS` and `ACDC` are also accepted.
- An invalid argument raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `DC`, `ACRMS` or `ACDC`.
commands.example:
:DVM:MODE ACRM    /*Selects AC rms.*/
:DVM:MODE?    /*The query returns ACRMS.*/

commands.desc: Queries the current reading of the digital voltmeter, in volts.
remarks: - `9.9E37` is returned when the source channel is off or no reading is available.
commands.returns: The query returns the voltage in scientific notation, for example `1.650000E+00`.
commands.example: :DVM:CURR?    /*The query returns 1.650000E+00.*/

subsystems.title: :COUNter Commands
subsystems.intro: The :COUNter commands control the frequency counter and query its reading.

commands.desc: Turns on or off the frequency counter, or queries its status.
remarks: - While the counter is on, its reading is also listed by :MEASure:STRip?.
- An invalid argument raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` or `0`.
commands.example:
:COUN:ENAB ON    /*Turns on the counter.*/
:COUN:ENAB?    /*The query returns 1.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the source of the frequency counter.
remarks: - Only analog channels are accepted; references are not.
- An invalid argument raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `CHAN<n>`.
commands.example:
:COUN:SOUR CHAN1    /*Sets the counter source to CH1.*/
:COUN:SOUR?    /*The query returns CHAN1.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the measurement mode of the frequency counter: frequency, period or totalize (edge count).
remarks: - An invalid argument raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `FREQ`, `PER` or `TOT`.
commands.example:
:COUN:MODE PER    /*Selects period mode.*/
:COUN:MODE?    /*The query returns PER.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the number of digits shown by the frequency counter.
remarks: - A value outside 3 to 7 raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns an integer, for example `6`.
commands.example:
:COUN:NDIG 6    /*Shows 6 digits.*/
:COUN:NDIG?    /*The query returns 6.*/

commands.desc: Queries the current reading of the frequency counter.
remarks: - The unit depends on :COUNter:MODE: Hz (frequency), s (period) or a number of edges (totalize).
- `9.9E37` is returned when the counter is off, the source channel is off, or no reading is available.
commands.returns: The query returns the reading in scientific notation, for example `1.000000E+06`.
commands.example: :COUN:CURR?    /*The query returns 1.000000E+06.*/

commands.desc: Clears the totalized count and the counter statistics.
commands.example: :COUN:TOT:CLE    /*Clears the totalized count.*/

subsystems.title: :HISTogram Commands
subsystems.intro: The :HISTogram commands control the waveform histogram and query its statistics.

commands.desc: Turns on or off the histogram, or queries its status.
remarks: - Turning the histogram on while it is off selects a vertical histogram.
- An invalid argument raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` or `0`.
commands.example:
:HIST:ENAB ON    /*Turns on the histogram.*/
:HIST:ENAB?    /*The query returns 1.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the histogram type: horizontal (time distribution) or vertical (voltage distribution).
remarks: - Setting a type also turns the histogram on.
- The query returns `VERT` also while the histogram is off.
- An invalid argument raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `HOR` or `VERT`.
commands.example:
:HIST:TYPE HOR    /*Selects a horizontal histogram.*/
:HIST:TYPE?    /*The query returns HOR.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the source of the histogram.
remarks: - The histogram uses the measurement source A. Setting the histogram source turns that channel on and makes it the :MEASure:SOURce A selection.
- The query returns the measurement source when that channel is on, otherwise the first channel that is on, or `CHAN1` when no channel is on.
- Only analog channels are accepted. An invalid argument raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `CHAN<n>`.
commands.example:
:HIST:SOUR CHAN1    /*Sets the histogram source to CH1.*/
:HIST:SOUR?    /*The query returns CHAN1.*/

commands.desc: Queries the statistics of the histogram.
remarks: - The statistics describe the histogram as displayed, for the current view and zoom, not every sample of the full record.
- Values are in volts for a vertical histogram and in seconds for a horizontal histogram.
- Undefined figures are returned as `9.9E37`. While the histogram is off, the reply is `Sum:0,Peaks:0` followed by `9.9E37` for every other figure.
commands.returns: The query returns `Sum:<n>,Peaks:<n>,Max:<v>,Min:<v>,Pk_Pk:<v>,Mean:<v>,Median:<v>,Mode:<v>,Bin width:<v>,Sigma:<v>`, where `<n>` is an integer and `<v>` is in scientific notation.

subsystems.title: :MASK Commands
subsystems.intro: The :MASK commands control the pass/fail mask test and query its results.

commands.desc: Turns on or off the pass/fail mask test, or queries its status.
remarks: - An invalid argument raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` or `0`.
commands.example:
:MASK:ENAB ON    /*Turns on the mask test.*/
:MASK:ENAB?    /*The query returns 1.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the source of the mask test.
remarks: - Only analog channels are accepted; references and math are not.
- An invalid argument raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `CHAN<n>`.
commands.example:
:MASK:SOUR CHAN1    /*Sets the mask source to CH1.*/
:MASK:SOUR?    /*The query returns CHAN1.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the horizontal tolerance of the mask, in divisions.
remarks: - If a mask has already been created, it is rebuilt with the new tolerance.
- A value out of range raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the tolerance in scientific notation, for example `2.000000E-01`.
commands.example:
:MASK:X 0.24    /*Sets the horizontal tolerance to 0.24 div.*/
:MASK:X?    /*The query returns 2.400000E-01.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the vertical tolerance of the mask, in divisions.
remarks: - If a mask has already been created, it is rebuilt with the new tolerance.
- A value out of range raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns the tolerance in scientific notation, for example `4.000000E-01`.
commands.example:
:MASK:Y 0.48    /*Sets the vertical tolerance to 0.48 div.*/
:MASK:Y?    /*The query returns 4.800000E-01.*/

commands.desc: Creates the mask from the source channel of the displayed record, using the current X and Y tolerances.
remarks: - If the source has no waveform, `-230,"Data corrupt or stale" source has no waveform` is raised.
commands.example: :MASK:CRE    /*Creates the mask.*/

commands.desc: Resets the pass, fail and total counts of the mask test to zero.
commands.example: :MASK:RES    /*Resets the mask test counts.*/

commands.desc: Starts or stops the mask test (runs or stops the acquisition), or queries its state.
remarks: - The mask test must be enabled (:MASK:ENABle ON); otherwise `-224,"Illegal parameter value" mask is off` is raised.
- `RUN` starts the acquisition; if the trigger sweep is Single it is changed to Auto. `STOP` stops the acquisition.
- An invalid argument raises `-224,"Illegal parameter value"`.
commands.returns: The query returns `RUN` when the mask test is enabled and the acquisition is running, otherwise `STOP`.
commands.example:
:MASK:OPER RUN    /*Starts the mask test.*/
:MASK:OPER?    /*The query returns RUN.*/

commands.desc: Queries the number of failed waveforms of the mask test.
commands.returns: The query returns an integer, for example `12`.
commands.example: :MASK:FAIL?    /*The query returns 12.*/

commands.desc: Queries the number of passed waveforms of the mask test.
commands.returns: The query returns an integer, for example `4988`.
commands.example: :MASK:PASS?    /*The query returns 4988.*/

commands.desc: Queries the total number of tested waveforms (passed + failed) of the mask test.
commands.returns: The query returns an integer, for example `5000`.
commands.example: :MASK:TOT?    /*The query returns 5000.*/

subsystems.title: :MATH Commands
subsystems.intro: The :MATH<n> commands configure the eight math traces (MATH1 to MATH8). Each trace combines one or two sources with an arithmetic, logic, FFT, filter or user-defined expression operator. A trace is displayed whenever its operator is not OFF.

commands.desc: Turns the specified math trace on or off, or queries its display status. Turning the trace off sets its operator to OFF; turning it on from OFF selects ADD, otherwise the current operator is kept.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` when the operator of the trace is not OFF; otherwise it returns `0`.
commands.example:
:MATH1:DISP ON    /*Turns on MATH1 (operator ADD if it was off).*/
:MATH1:DISP?    /*The query returns 1.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the operator of the specified math trace. Setting an operator also turns the trace on. OFF is not accepted as an operator; use :MATH<n>:DISPlay OFF instead.
remarks: - AXB is the linear operator A×x+B. EXPR evaluates the formula set with :MATH<n>:EXPRession.
commands.returns: The query returns OFF, ADD, SUBT, MULT, DIV, AND, OR, XOR, NOT, NAND, NOR, FFT, INTG, DIFF, SQRT, LG, LN, EXP, ABS, LPAS, HPAS, BPAS, BST, AXB, CONV, FIR, EXPR, A2D, D2A or UNNRZI.
commands.example:
:MATH1:OPER SUBT    /*Sets the MATH1 operator to A-B.*/
:MATH1:OPER?    /*The query returns SUBT.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries source A (the first source) of the specified math trace.
remarks: - A source may be an analog channel available on the model, a loaded reference R1 to R10 (`REF<n>` is accepted as an alias on input), or an earlier math trace `MATH<m>` with m < n. A math trace cannot use itself or a later trace as a source.
- Selecting an empty reference slot is rejected with error -230,"Math reference source is empty".
- Reference sources keep their own recorded timing; a math result is only meaningful where the sources overlap in physical time.
commands.returns: The query returns CHAN<n>, MATH<m> or R<n>.
commands.example:
:MATH2:SOUR1 MATH1    /*Uses MATH1 as source A of MATH2.*/
:MATH2:SOUR1?    /*The query returns MATH1.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries source B (the second source) of the specified math trace. Source B is used by two-operand operators.
remarks: - A source may be an analog channel available on the model, a loaded reference R1 to R10 (`REF<n>` is accepted as an alias on input), or an earlier math trace `MATH<m>` with m < n. A math trace cannot use itself or a later trace as a source.
- Selecting an empty reference slot is rejected with error -230,"Math reference source is empty".
- Reference sources keep their own recorded timing; a math result is only meaningful where the sources overlap in physical time.
commands.returns: The query returns CHAN<n>, MATH<m> or R<n>.
commands.example:
:MATH1:SOUR2 R1    /*Uses reference R1 as source B of MATH1.*/
:MATH1:SOUR2?    /*The query returns R1.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the vertical scale of the specified math trace. The value is rounded to the nearest step of the 1-2-5 sequence from 1e-9 to 5e9 units/div; when the operator is FFT, it is rounded to the nearest of 1, 2, 5, 10 and 20 dB/div.
params: 1e-9 to 5e9 (FFT: 1 to 20 dB/div); must be greater than 0
commands.returns: The query returns the scale in a real number in scientific notation with seven significant digits (for example `1.000000E+00`); `9.9E37` when the value is unavailable.
commands.example:
:MATH1:SCAL 0.5    /*Sets the MATH1 scale to 500 mV/div.*/
:MATH1:SCAL?    /*The query returns 5.000000E-01.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the vertical offset of the specified math trace. Values outside the range are clipped to the range limit.
commands.returns: The query returns the offset in a real number in scientific notation with seven significant digits (for example `1.000000E+00`); `9.9E37` when the value is unavailable.
commands.example:
:MATH1:OFFS -0.2    /*Sets the MATH1 offset to -200 mV.*/
:MATH1:OFFS?    /*The query returns -2.000000E-01.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the user-defined formula of the specified math trace. Setting a formula also selects the EXPR operator. The formula is checked when it is sent; an invalid formula is rejected and the previous one is kept.
params: Formula in single or double quotes; source names CH1 to CH4, M1 to M8 and R1 to R10
remarks: - Reference names in a formula (for example `R1 - R2`) require the slots to be loaded for the result to be computed.
commands.returns: The query returns the formula text without quotes.
commands.example:
:MATH3:EXPR "CH1 - CH2"    /*Sets the MATH3 formula and selects EXPR.*/
:MATH3:EXPR?    /*The query returns CH1 - CH2.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the FFT source of the specified math trace. Setting the source also selects the FFT operator. The FFT source is the same setting as source A (:MATH<n>:SOURce1).
remarks: - A source may be an analog channel available on the model, a loaded reference R1 to R10 (`REF<n>` is accepted as an alias on input), or an earlier math trace `MATH<m>` with m < n. A math trace cannot use itself or a later trace as a source.
- Selecting an empty reference slot is rejected with error -230,"Math reference source is empty".
commands.returns: The query returns CHAN<n>, MATH<m> or R<n>.
commands.example:
:MATH1:FFT:SOUR CHAN2    /*Selects an FFT of CH2 on MATH1.*/
:MATH1:FFT:SOUR?    /*The query returns CHAN2.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the window function applied to the FFT of the specified math trace.
commands.returns: The query returns RECT, BLAC, HANN, HAMM or FLAT.
commands.example:
:MATH1:FFT:WIND FLAT    /*Selects the flat-top window.*/
:MATH1:FFT:WIND?    /*The query returns FLAT.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the vertical scale of the FFT of the specified math trace in dB/div. The value is rounded to the nearest of 1, 2, 5, 10 and 20 dB/div. Setting the scale also selects the FFT operator.
remarks: - This scale shares its setting with :MATH<n>:SCALe. The query reads the setting as a dB value even when the operator is not FFT.
commands.returns: The query returns the scale in dB/div in a real number in scientific notation with seven significant digits (for example `1.000000E+00`); `9.9E37` when the value is unavailable.
commands.example:
:MATH1:FFT:SCAL 20    /*Sets the FFT scale to 20 dB/div.*/
:MATH1:FFT:SCAL?    /*The query returns 2.000000E+01.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the filter type of the specified math trace. Setting a type also sets the operator of the trace to that filter.
commands.returns: The query returns LPAS, HPAS, BPAS or BST. It returns LPAS when the operator is not a filter.
commands.example:
:MATH1:FILT:TYPE BPAS    /*Sets MATH1 to a band-pass filter.*/
:MATH1:FILT:TYPE?    /*The query returns BPAS.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the corner frequency of a low-pass, high-pass or FIR operator, or the lower band edge of a band-pass or band-stop filter, in Hz.
params: Greater than 0; for band filters lower than W2
remarks: - When the operator has no corner frequency, the command generates error -221,"Settings conflict" and the query returns `9.9E37`.
- For band filters, a W1 value equal to or above W2 generates error -221,"Settings conflict".
commands.returns: The query returns the frequency in a real number in scientific notation with seven significant digits (for example `1.000000E+00`); `9.9E37` when the value is unavailable.
commands.example:
:MATH1:FILT:W1 1000    /*Sets the lower band edge to 1 kHz.*/
:MATH1:FILT:W1?    /*The query returns 1.000000E+03.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the upper band edge of a band-pass or band-stop filter of the specified math trace, in Hz.
remarks: - W2 applies to band filters only. For any other operator the command generates error -221,"Settings conflict" and the query returns `9.9E37`.
commands.returns: The query returns the frequency in a real number in scientific notation with seven significant digits (for example `1.000000E+00`); `9.9E37` when the value is unavailable.
commands.example:
:MATH1:FILT:W2 5000    /*Sets the upper band edge to 5 kHz.*/
:MATH1:FILT:W2?    /*The query returns 5.000000E+03.*/

subsystems.title: :DECode Commands
subsystems.intro: The :DECode commands configure the protocol decoder that is currently selected (one of four decoder slots) and read its decoded events. Source roles may be analog channels, loaded references or, with LA input, digital lines. The :DECode subsystem is an OOS extension; the :BUS<n> commands address a slot directly.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the decoder slot that the other :DECode commands act on.
commands.returns: The query returns an integer from 1 to 4.
commands.example:
:DEC:SEL 2    /*Selects decoder slot 2.*/
:DEC:SEL?    /*The query returns 2.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the protocol of the selected decoder. The name is matched ignoring case, spaces and punctuation, so `CAN-FD`, `canfd` and `CAN FD` are equivalent.
params: UART, I2C, SPI, CAN, LIN, I2S, 1553, Parallel, CAN-FD, FlexRay, DMX512, Modbus RTU, Modbus ASCII, 1-Wire, DS2482, UART 9-bit, SWD, JTAG, Quad-SPI, I3C, S/PDIF, USB PD, ARINC 429, SENT, USB, Manchester, MLT-3, C-PHY
remarks: - Selecting C-PHY also sets the decode threshold to 0.02 V and the input to WAVEFORM.
commands.returns: The query returns the protocol display name exactly as listed, in mixed case (for example `UART`, `CAN-FD`, `Modbus RTU`, `C-PHY`).
commands.example:
:DEC:PROT CANFD    /*Selects the CAN-FD protocol.*/
:DEC:PROT?    /*The query returns CAN-FD.*/

commands.desc: Turns the selected decoder on or off, or queries its status.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` or `0`.
commands.example:
:DEC:STAT ON    /*Turns on the selected decoder.*/
:DEC:STAT?    /*The query returns 1.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the decision threshold of the selected decoder in source units. For C-PHY, the value is the minimum level separation between adjacent wires.
commands.returns: The query returns the threshold in a real number in scientific notation with seven significant digits (for example `1.000000E+00`); `9.9E37` when the value is unavailable.
commands.example:
:DEC:THR 1.4    /*Sets the decoder threshold to 1.4 V.*/
:DEC:THR?    /*The query returns 1.400000E+00.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries whether the selected decoder reads analog waveforms or logic-analyzer lines. ANALOG is accepted as an alias of WAVEFORM.
remarks: - The tokens must be sent in full (no short forms).
- LA is accepted only when the logic analyzer is on and the protocol is not C-PHY; otherwise the command generates error -224.
commands.returns: The query returns WAVEFORM or LA.
commands.example:
:DEC:INP WAVEFORM    /*Decodes analog waveforms.*/
:DEC:INP?    /*The query returns WAVEFORM.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the first source role of the selected decoder (the main data line). The meaning of each role depends on the protocol.
remarks: - The command acts on the decoder selected with :DECode:SELect.
- Setting a channel or reference source switches the decoder input to WAVEFORM. When a Bus trigger is active, the trigger source follows the primary role.
- A reference role must be a loaded slot. Roles taken from references and acquired channels must overlap in physical time to decode.
commands.returns: The query returns CH<n> (not CHAN<n>), R<n>, NONE or Unavailable; with LA input it returns D<n> or NONE.
commands.example:
:DEC:SOUR CHAN1    /*Sets the first role to CH1.*/
:DEC:SOUR?    /*The query returns CH1.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the second source role of the selected decoder (typically the clock line).
remarks: - The command acts on the decoder selected with :DECode:SELect.
- Setting a channel or reference source switches the decoder input to WAVEFORM. When a Bus trigger is active, the trigger source follows the primary role.
- A reference role must be a loaded slot. Roles taken from references and acquired channels must overlap in physical time to decode.
commands.returns: The query returns CH<n> (not CHAN<n>), R<n>, NONE or Unavailable; with LA input it returns D<n> or NONE.
commands.example:
:DEC:SOUR2 R2    /*Sets the second role to reference R2.*/
:DEC:SOUR2?    /*The query returns R2.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the third source role of the selected decoder (for example SPI chip select). NONE removes the optional role.
remarks: - The command acts on the decoder selected with :DECode:SELect.
- Setting a channel or reference source switches the decoder input to WAVEFORM. When a Bus trigger is active, the trigger source follows the primary role.
- A reference role must be a loaded slot. Roles taken from references and acquired channels must overlap in physical time to decode.
- NONE is not accepted for C-PHY, which needs all three wires.
commands.returns: The query returns CH<n> (not CHAN<n>), R<n>, NONE or Unavailable; with LA input it returns D<n> or NONE.
commands.example:
:DEC:CS NONE    /*Removes the chip-select role.*/
:DEC:CS?    /*The query returns NONE.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the fourth source role of the selected decoder. NONE removes the optional role.
remarks: - The command acts on the decoder selected with :DECode:SELect.
- Setting a channel or reference source switches the decoder input to WAVEFORM. When a Bus trigger is active, the trigger source follows the primary role.
- A reference role must be a loaded slot. Roles taken from references and acquired channels must overlap in physical time to decode.
commands.returns: The query returns CH<n> (not CHAN<n>), R<n>, NONE or Unavailable; with LA input it returns D<n> or NONE.
commands.example:
:DEC:SOUR4 CHAN4    /*Sets the fourth role to CH4.*/
:DEC:SOUR4?    /*The query returns CH4.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the differential partner of the main source of the selected decoder. NONE decodes single-ended.
remarks: - The command acts on the decoder selected with :DECode:SELect.
- This role always uses a channel or reference, also when the input is LA.
- Setting a channel or reference source switches the decoder input to WAVEFORM. When a Bus trigger is active, the trigger source follows the primary role.
- A reference role must be a loaded slot. Roles taken from references and acquired channels must overlap in physical time to decode.
commands.returns: The query returns CH<n> (not CHAN<n>), R<n>, NONE or Unavailable.
commands.example:
:DEC:DIFF CHAN2    /*Uses CH2 as the negative leg.*/
:DEC:DIFF?    /*The query returns CH2.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the C-PHY symbol rate of the selected decoder in symbols/s. AUTO (or 0) derives the rate from the signal.
remarks: - An invalid rate generates error -224,"Invalid C-PHY symbol rate".
commands.returns: The query returns `AUTO`, or the rate in a real number in scientific notation with seven significant digits (for example `1.000000E+00`); `9.9E37` when the value is unavailable.
commands.example:
:DEC:CPHY:RATE 2.5e9    /*Sets the symbol rate to 2.5 Gsym/s.*/
:DEC:CPHY:RATE?    /*The query returns 2.500000E+09.*/

commands.desc: Queries whether decoding is still being computed in the background. The query does not change the acquisition.
remarks: - Poll this query until it returns `0` before reading :DECode:EVENts? on long records.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` while decoding is in progress and `0` otherwise.
commands.example: :DEC:BUSY?    /*The query returns 0.*/

commands.desc: Queries the decoded event table of all decoders. Each row is one event; rows are separated by line feeds inside the reply.
remarks: - While decoding is still computing, the query returns the plain text `BUSY`.
- When decoding cannot run (for example an unavailable source), the query generates error -230 with the decoder's reason.
- Times are in seconds of physical time on the record's time axis.
commands.returns: The query returns rows in time order in the format `<time>,<decoder>,<text>,<status>`. <time> is in seconds in short exponent form (for example `1.25e-6`); <decoder> is the slot, protocol name and main source, for example `D1 UART CH1` (without the source when the input is LA); <text> is the decoded content as shown in the event table; <status> is `ok` or `error`. The reply is empty when no decoder is on or nothing was decoded.
commands.example: :DEC:EVEN?    /*The query returns 1.25e-6,D1 UART CH1,0x41,ok (one row per event).*/

subsystems.title: :BUS Commands
subsystems.intro: The :BUS<n> commands configure decoder slots 1 to 4 by number, independently of the slot selected with :DECode:SELect. RS232 refers to the UART decoder.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the protocol of the specified decoder slot.
params: {PARallel|RS232|UART|IIC|I2C|LIN|SPI|CAN}, or a compact token: I2S, 1553, CANFD, FLEXRAY, DMX512, MODBUSRTU, MODBUSASCII, 1WIRE, DS2482, UART9BIT, SWD, JTAG, QUADSPI, I3C, SPDIF, USBPD, ARINC429, SENT, USB, MANCHESTER, MLT3, CPHY
commands.returns: The query returns PAR, RS232, SPI, IIC, LIN, CAN, or the compact upper-case token for other protocols (for example CANFD).
commands.example:
:BUS1:MODE SPI    /*Sets decoder 1 to SPI.*/
:BUS1:MODE?    /*The query returns SPI.*/

commands.desc: Turns the specified decoder on or off, or queries its status.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` or `0`.
commands.example:
:BUS1:DISP ON    /*Turns on decoder 1.*/
:BUS1:DISP?    /*The query returns 1.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the display format of the decoded data of the specified decoder.
commands.returns: The query returns HEX or ASC.
commands.example:
:BUS1:FORM HEX    /*Shows decoded data in hexadecimal.*/
:BUS1:FORM?    /*The query returns HEX.*/

commands.desc: Shows or hides the decode event table, or queries its status. The event table is one window shared by all decoders, so the setting is the same for every <n>.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` or `0`.
commands.example:
:BUS1:EVEN ON    /*Opens the event table.*/
:BUS1:EVEN?    /*The query returns 1.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the decision threshold of the specified decoder in source units. When several comma-separated values are sent, only the last one is used.
commands.returns: The query returns the threshold in a real number in scientific notation with seven significant digits (for example `1.000000E+00`); `9.9E37` when the value is unavailable.
commands.example:
:BUS1:THR 0.9    /*Sets the decoder 1 threshold to 0.9 V.*/
:BUS1:THR?    /*The query returns 9.000000E-01.*/

commands.desc: Queries the decoded events of the specified decoder.
remarks: - While decoding is still computing, the query returns the plain text `BUSY` (not a block). Poll :DECode:BUSY? first.
- When decoding cannot run, the query generates error -230 with the decoder's reason.
commands.returns: The query returns an IEEE 488.2 definite-length block (`#9` followed by nine length digits). Its content is the protocol token (as returned by :BUS<n>:MODE?) and a line feed, followed by the event rows of this decoder in the :DECode:EVENts? row format, separated by line feeds.
commands.example: :BUS1:DATA?    /*The query returns #9000000033 followed by RS232, a line feed and 1.25e-6,D1 UART CH1,0x41,ok*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the TX source of the UART decoder in the specified slot. Setting a source also sets the slot protocol to UART.
remarks: - A reference source must be a loaded slot; otherwise the command generates error -224,"Decoder source is unavailable".
- Configuring slot <n> does not change which decoder is selected or shown.
commands.returns: The query returns CHAN<n>, R<n> or Unavailable. Note that this differs from :DECode:SOURce?, which returns CH<n>.
commands.example:
:BUS1:RS232:TX CHAN1    /*Sets the TX source to CH1.*/
:BUS1:RS232:TX?    /*The query returns CHAN1.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the RX source of the UART decoder in the specified slot. Setting a source also sets the slot protocol to UART.
remarks: - A reference source must be a loaded slot; otherwise the command generates error -224,"Decoder source is unavailable".
- Configuring slot <n> does not change which decoder is selected or shown.
- UART decoding uses the configured primary input (TX).
commands.returns: The query returns CHAN<n>, R<n> or Unavailable. Note that this differs from :DECode:SOURce?, which returns CH<n>.
commands.example:
:BUS1:RS232:RX CHAN2    /*Sets the RX source to CH2.*/
:BUS1:RS232:RX?    /*The query returns CHAN2.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the baud rate of the UART decoder. The value is rounded to the nearest supported rate. Setting it also sets the slot protocol to UART.
commands.returns: The query returns the baud rate as an integer.
commands.example:
:BUS1:RS232:BAUD 9600    /*Sets 9600 baud.*/
:BUS1:RS232:BAUD?    /*The query returns 9600.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the parity of the UART decoder. Setting it also sets the slot protocol to UART.
commands.returns: The query returns NONE, ODD or EVEN.
commands.example:
:BUS1:RS232:PAR EVEN    /*Sets even parity.*/
:BUS1:RS232:PAR?    /*The query returns EVEN.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the number of data bits of the UART decoder. Setting it also sets the slot protocol to UART.
remarks: - UART and SPI share one word-length setting per slot.
commands.returns: The query returns an integer.
commands.example:
:BUS1:RS232:DBIT 7    /*Sets 7 data bits.*/
:BUS1:RS232:DBIT?    /*The query returns 7.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the clock (SCL) source of the I2C decoder in the specified slot. Setting a source also sets the slot protocol to I2C.
remarks: - A reference source must be a loaded slot; otherwise the command generates error -224,"Decoder source is unavailable".
- Configuring slot <n> does not change which decoder is selected or shown.
commands.returns: The query returns CHAN<n>, R<n> or Unavailable. Note that this differs from :DECode:SOURce?, which returns CH<n>.
commands.example:
:BUS2:IIC:SCLK:SOUR CHAN1    /*Sets SCL to CH1.*/
:BUS2:IIC:SCLK:SOUR?    /*The query returns CHAN1.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the data (SDA) source of the I2C decoder in the specified slot. Setting a source also sets the slot protocol to I2C.
remarks: - A reference source must be a loaded slot; otherwise the command generates error -224,"Decoder source is unavailable".
- Configuring slot <n> does not change which decoder is selected or shown.
commands.returns: The query returns CHAN<n>, R<n> or Unavailable. Note that this differs from :DECode:SOURce?, which returns CH<n>.
commands.example:
:BUS2:IIC:SDA:SOUR CHAN2    /*Sets SDA to CH2.*/
:BUS2:IIC:SDA:SOUR?    /*The query returns CHAN2.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the clock source of the SPI decoder in the specified slot. Setting a source also sets the slot protocol to SPI.
remarks: - A reference source must be a loaded slot; otherwise the command generates error -224,"Decoder source is unavailable".
- Configuring slot <n> does not change which decoder is selected or shown.
commands.returns: The query returns CHAN<n>, R<n> or Unavailable. Note that this differs from :DECode:SOURce?, which returns CH<n>.
commands.example:
:BUS3:SPI:SCLK:SOUR CHAN1    /*Sets the SPI clock to CH1.*/
:BUS3:SPI:SCLK:SOUR?    /*The query returns CHAN1.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the MOSI data source of the SPI decoder in the specified slot. Setting a source also sets the slot protocol to SPI.
remarks: - A reference source must be a loaded slot; otherwise the command generates error -224,"Decoder source is unavailable".
- Configuring slot <n> does not change which decoder is selected or shown.
commands.returns: The query returns CHAN<n>, R<n> or Unavailable. Note that this differs from :DECode:SOURce?, which returns CH<n>.
commands.example:
:BUS3:SPI:MOSI:SOUR CHAN2    /*Sets MOSI to CH2.*/
:BUS3:SPI:MOSI:SOUR?    /*The query returns CHAN2.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the chip-select (SS) source of the SPI decoder in the specified slot. OFF or NONE decodes without chip select. Setting a source also sets the slot protocol to SPI.
remarks: - A reference source must be a loaded slot; otherwise the command generates error -224,"Decoder source is unavailable".
- Configuring slot <n> does not change which decoder is selected or shown.
commands.returns: The query returns CHAN<n>, R<n>, Unavailable, or OFF when no chip select is used.
commands.example:
:BUS3:SPI:SS:SOUR CHAN3    /*Sets chip select to CH3.*/
:BUS3:SPI:SS:SOUR?    /*The query returns CHAN3.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the word length of the SPI decoder. Setting it also sets the slot protocol to SPI.
remarks: - UART and SPI share one word-length setting per slot.
commands.returns: The query returns an integer.
commands.example:
:BUS3:SPI:DBIT 16    /*Sets 16-bit SPI words.*/
:BUS3:SPI:DBIT?    /*The query returns 16.*/

subsystems.title: :LA Commands
subsystems.intro: The :LA commands control the 16-line logic analyzer (D0 to D15) in two pods and read its last record. Availability depends on the model.

commands.desc: Turns the logic analyzer on or off, or queries its status.
remarks: - On a model without a logic-analyzer port, every :LA command generates error -241,"Hardware missing".
commands.returns: The query returns `1` or `0`.
commands.example:
:LA:STAT ON    /*Turns on the logic analyzer.*/
:LA:STAT?    /*The query returns 1.*/

commands.desc: Shows or hides the specified digital line, or queries its display status.
remarks: - On a model without a logic-analyzer port, every :LA command generates error -241,"Hardware missing".
commands.returns: The query returns `1` or `0`.
commands.example:
:LA:DIG3:DISP ON    /*Shows line D3.*/
:LA:DIG3:DISP?    /*The query returns 1.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the logic threshold of the specified pod (POD1 = D0 to D7, POD2 = D8 to D15) in volts. Setting a value switches the pod to a user-defined threshold.
remarks: - On a model without a logic-analyzer port, every :LA command generates error -241,"Hardware missing".
commands.returns: The query returns the threshold in short exponent form without padding (for example `1.5e0` or `-2e-1`), which differs from the usual seven-digit format.
commands.example:
:LA:POD1:THR 1.5    /*Sets the POD1 threshold to 1.5 V.*/
:LA:POD1:THR?    /*The query returns 1.5e0.*/

commands.desc: Queries the number of samples in the last logic-analyzer record.
remarks: - On a model without a logic-analyzer port, every :LA command generates error -241,"Hardware missing".
- When no record exists, the query returns `0` and generates error -230,"Data corrupt or stale".
commands.returns: The query returns an integer.
commands.example: :LA:POIN?    /*The query returns 100000.*/

commands.desc: Queries the format of the last logic-analyzer record: the sample count, the sample interval and the time of the first sample.
remarks: - On a model without a logic-analyzer port, every :LA command generates error -241,"Hardware missing".
- When no record exists, the query returns `0` and generates error -230,"Data corrupt or stale".
commands.returns: The query returns `<points>,<dt>,<t0>`; <dt> and <t0> are in seconds in short exponent form (for example `1e-8`).
commands.example: :LA:PRE?    /*The query returns 100000,1e-8,-5e-4.*/

commands.desc: Queries the samples of the last logic-analyzer record.
remarks: - On a model without a logic-analyzer port, every :LA command generates error -241,"Hardware missing".
- When no record exists, the query returns an empty block `#9000000000` and generates error -230,"Data corrupt or stale".
commands.returns: The query returns an IEEE 488.2 definite-length block of 16-bit little-endian words, one per sample; bit n of each word is line Dn.
commands.example: :LA:DATA?    /*The query returns #9000200000 followed by 200000 bytes (100000 words).*/

subsystems.title: :REFerence Commands
subsystems.intro: The :REFerence commands manage the ten reference slots R1 to R10. A slot holds a stored waveform with its own native timing, either copied from a channel or loaded from a file on the instrument. Most commands act on the working slot unless a slot prefix is given.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the working (destination) slot that reference commands act on by default.
commands.returns: The query returns R<n>.
commands.example:
:REF:SLOT R3    /*Makes R3 the working slot.*/
:REF:SLOT?    /*The query returns R3.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the current reference slot. This is the same setting as :REFerence:SLOT, returned as a number.
commands.returns: The query returns an integer from 1 to 10.
commands.example:
:REF:CURR 3    /*Makes R3 the working slot.*/
:REF:CURR?    /*The query returns 3.*/

commands.desc: Shows or hides a loaded reference slot, or queries whether it is displayed. Setting also makes the slot the working slot.
remarks: - The optional slot prefix (for example `R2,`) selects the slot; without it the working slot (:REFerence:SLOT) is used. When the value itself starts with a digit or with R, include the slot prefix, because a bare value is otherwise read as a slot.
- Showing or hiding an empty slot generates error -224,"Illegal parameter value".
commands.returns: The query returns `1` if the slot is loaded and displayed, otherwise `0`.
commands.example:
:REF:SHOW R2,ON    /*Shows reference R2.*/
:REF:SHOW? R2    /*The query returns 1.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the channel that :REFerence:SAVE copies into the slot. Setting also makes the slot the working slot.
remarks: - The optional slot prefix (for example `R2,`) selects the slot; without it the working slot (:REFerence:SLOT) is used. When the value itself starts with a digit or with R, include the slot prefix, because a bare value is otherwise read as a slot.
commands.returns: The query returns CHAN<n>.
commands.example:
:REF:SOUR R1,CHAN2    /*R1 copies CH2 on the next save.*/
:REF:SOUR? R1    /*The query returns CHAN2.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the display scale of a loaded reference in V/div. The stored samples are not changed. Setting also makes the slot the working slot.
params: Greater than 0 (any value, no step sequence)
remarks: - The optional slot prefix (for example `R2,`) selects the slot; without it the working slot (:REFerence:SLOT) is used. When the value itself starts with a digit or with R, include the slot prefix, because a bare value is otherwise read as a slot.
- If the slot is empty, the command generates error -230,"Data corrupt or stale" reference is empty.
commands.returns: The query returns the scale in a real number in scientific notation with seven significant digits (for example `1.000000E+00`); `9.9E37` when the value is unavailable.
commands.example:
:REF:VSC R1,0.2    /*Sets R1 to 200 mV/div.*/
:REF:VSC? R1    /*The query returns 2.000000E-01.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the display offset of a loaded reference in volts. The stored samples are not changed. Setting also makes the slot the working slot.
remarks: - The optional slot prefix (for example `R2,`) selects the slot; without it the working slot (:REFerence:SLOT) is used. When the value itself starts with a digit or with R, include the slot prefix, because a bare value is otherwise read as a slot.
- If the slot is empty, the command generates error -230,"Data corrupt or stale" reference is empty.
commands.returns: The query returns the offset in a real number in scientific notation with seven significant digits (for example `1.000000E+00`); `9.9E37` when the value is unavailable.
commands.example:
:REF:VOFF R1,-0.1    /*Sets the R1 offset to -100 mV.*/
:REF:VOFF? R1    /*The query returns -1.000000E-01.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the label text of a loaded reference.
remarks: - The optional slot prefix (for example `R2,`) selects the slot; without it the working slot (:REFerence:SLOT) is used. When the value itself starts with a digit or with R, include the slot prefix, because a bare value is otherwise read as a slot.
- If the slot is empty, the command generates error -230,"Data corrupt or stale" reference is empty.
commands.returns: The query returns the label text without quotes.
commands.example:
:REF:LAB:CONT R1,"Golden"    /*Labels R1 as Golden.*/
:REF:LAB:CONT? R1    /*The query returns Golden.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the display color of a loaded reference. WHITe is accepted for GRAY; ORANge and VIOLet select the same fifth color, which is drawn as violet.
remarks: - The optional slot prefix (for example `R2,`) selects the slot; without it the working slot (:REFerence:SLOT) is used. When the value itself starts with a digit or with R, include the slot prefix, because a bare value is otherwise read as a slot.
- If the slot is empty, the command generates error -230,"Data corrupt or stale" reference is empty.
commands.returns: The query returns GRAY, RED, GRE, BLUE or ORAN.
commands.example:
:REF:COL R1,RED    /*Draws R1 in red.*/
:REF:COL? R1    /*The query returns RED.*/

commands.desc: Resets the display scale and offset of a loaded reference: the offset to 0 and the scale to the V/div of its source channel. Recorded samples and timing are retained.
remarks: - If the slot is empty, the command generates error -230,"Data corrupt or stale" reference is empty.
commands.example: :REF:RES R1    /*Resets the R1 scale and offset.*/

commands.desc: Empties all ten reference slots.
remarks: - Math traces, decoders and measurements that use a reference become unavailable until the slot is loaded again.
commands.example: :REF:CLE    /*Clears R1 to R10.*/

commands.desc: Copies the current record of the :REFerence:SOURce channel into the working slot. When a slot is given, it is made the working slot first. No file is written.
remarks: - If the source channel has no data, the command generates error -224,"Illegal parameter value" source channel has no data.
commands.example:
:REF:SOUR R2,CHAN1
:REF:SAVE R2    /*Stores the CH1 record in R2.*/

commands.desc: Loads a waveform file into the working slot. Supported formats are CSV, BIN, WFM, TRC, ISF, TR0 and WFMX.
params: Absolute path, or a path relative to the setup directory, in quotes
remarks: - The path refers to the file system of the instrument running OOS, not of the remote client. To use a file from the client, upload it through the UI.
- A missing file generates error -256,"File name not found"; an unreadable file generates error -224 with the reason.
- Loading a file is not an acquisition; the loaded record keeps its own native timing.
commands.example:
:REF:SLOT R1
:REF:LOAD "D:/captures/lane0.wfm"    /*Loads the file into R1.*/

commands.desc: Loads a waveform file into the working slot. With a path it behaves like :REFerence:LOAD. Without a path it loads `ref<n>` (n = working slot number) from the setup directory, trying the extensions wfm, bin, csv, trc, isf, tr0 and wfmx in that order.
remarks: - The path and the setup directory are on the instrument running OOS, not on the remote client.
- A missing file generates error -256,"File name not found".
commands.example:
:REF:SLOT R2
:REF:IMP    /*Loads ref2.wfm (or the first existing ref2.* file) into R2.*/

subsystems.title: :SIM Commands
subsystems.intro: The :SIM commands drive the built-in serial-link simulator, which generates high-speed lane waveforms (PRBS pattern with spread-spectrum clocking and jitter) into a reference slot. The :SIM subsystem is an OOS extension.

commands.desc: Sets or queries the lane preset. Selecting a preset cancels any generation in progress and copies the preset's pattern, spread-spectrum and jitter values into the :SIM settings.
params: {PCIe 1.0|PCIe 2.0|PCIe 3.0|PCIe 4.0|PCIe 5.0|USB 2.0 HS|USB 3.2 Gen 1|USB 3.2 Gen 2|SATA I|SATA II|SATA III|10GBASE-KR}, case-insensitive, in quotes
remarks: - The name must match exactly apart from case, including spaces.
commands.returns: The query returns the lane name exactly as listed, without quotes.
commands.example:
:SIM:PRES "USB 3.2 Gen 1"    /*Selects the USB 3.2 Gen 1 lane.*/
:SIM:PRES?    /*The query returns USB 3.2 Gen 1.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the reference slot that receives the generated waveform. Changing the slot cancels any generation in progress.
commands.returns: The query returns R<n>.
commands.example:
:SIM:SLOT R4    /*Generates into R4.*/
:SIM:SLOT?    /*The query returns R4.*/

commands.desc: Starts or stops simulated acquisition, or queries its status. ON (or no argument) applies the current :SIM settings and starts generating new records; OFF cancels generation, keeps the last accepted record and sets the acquisition to Stop.
remarks: - If generation cannot start, the command generates error -224 with the reason.
- Generation runs in the background; poll :SIM:BUSY?.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` or `0`.
commands.example:
:SIM:PLAY ON    /*Starts generating the selected lane.*/
:SIM:PLAY?    /*The query returns 1.*/

commands.desc: Shows or hides the reference slot that holds the simulated waveform, or queries whether it is displayed.
remarks: - If the slot is empty, the command generates error -224,"Illegal parameter value".
commands.returns: The query returns `1` if the slot is loaded and displayed, otherwise `0`.
commands.example:
:SIM:SHOW ON    /*Shows the simulated waveform.*/
:SIM:SHOW?    /*The query returns 1.*/

commands.desc: Queries whether background generation is running.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` while generation is running and `0` otherwise.
commands.example: :SIM:BUSY?    /*The query returns 0.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the PRBS pattern order. The PRBS prefix and the hyphen are optional, so `31`, `PRBS31` and `PRBS-31` are equivalent.
remarks: - Another order generates error -224,"Illegal parameter value" PRBS order.
commands.returns: The query returns PRBS<n>.
commands.example:
:SIM:PATT PRBS15    /*Selects PRBS15.*/
:SIM:PATT?    /*The query returns PRBS15.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the spread-spectrum clocking mode: off, down-spread or center-spread.
remarks: - The tokens are matched exactly (case-insensitive); other abbreviations are rejected with error -224,"Illegal parameter value" SSC mode.
commands.returns: The query returns OFF, DOWN or CENTER (long form).
commands.example:
:SIM:SSC:MODE CENT    /*Selects center spread.*/
:SIM:SSC:MODE?    /*The query returns CENTER.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the spread-spectrum deviation as a fraction (0.005 = 5000 ppm).
remarks: - A value outside the range generates error -224,"Illegal parameter value" SIM setting; the value is not clipped.
commands.returns: The query returns the deviation in a real number in scientific notation with seven significant digits (for example `1.000000E+00`); `9.9E37` when the value is unavailable.
commands.example:
:SIM:SSC:DEV 0.005    /*Sets 0.5 % deviation.*/
:SIM:SSC:DEV?    /*The query returns 5.000000E-03.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the spread-spectrum modulation frequency in Hz.
remarks: - A value outside the range generates error -224,"Illegal parameter value" SIM setting; the value is not clipped.
commands.returns: The query returns the frequency in a real number in scientific notation with seven significant digits (for example `1.000000E+00`); `9.9E37` when the value is unavailable.
commands.example:
:SIM:SSC:FREQ 33000    /*Sets 33 kHz modulation.*/
:SIM:SSC:FREQ?    /*The query returns 3.300000E+04.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the duty-cycle distortion added to the simulated signal, in seconds peak-to-peak.
remarks: - A value outside the range generates error -224,"Illegal parameter value" SIM setting; the value is not clipped.
commands.returns: The query returns the value in a real number in scientific notation with seven significant digits (for example `1.000000E+00`); `9.9E37` when the value is unavailable.
commands.example:
:SIM:JITT:DCD 5e-12    /*Adds 5 ps p-p DCD.*/
:SIM:JITT:DCD?    /*The query returns 5.000000E-12.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the RMS amplitude of correlated (band-limited) random jitter, in seconds.
remarks: - A value outside the range generates error -224,"Illegal parameter value" SIM setting; the value is not clipped.
commands.returns: The query returns the value in a real number in scientific notation with seven significant digits (for example `1.000000E+00`); `9.9E37` when the value is unavailable.
commands.example:
:SIM:JITT:CORR 1e-12    /*Adds 1 ps RMS correlated jitter.*/
:SIM:JITT:CORR?    /*The query returns 1.000000E-12.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the corner frequency of the correlated jitter in Hz.
remarks: - A value outside the range generates error -224,"Illegal parameter value" SIM setting; the value is not clipped.
commands.returns: The query returns the frequency in a real number in scientific notation with seven significant digits (for example `1.000000E+00`); `9.9E37` when the value is unavailable.
commands.example:
:SIM:JITT:CORN 2e6    /*Sets a 2 MHz corner.*/
:SIM:JITT:CORN?    /*The query returns 2.000000E+06.*/

subsystems.title: :SOURce Commands
subsystems.intro: The :SOURce[<n>] commands control the built-in function/arbitrary waveform generator on models that have one. <n> selects the generator and may be omitted for generator 1.

commands.desc: Turns the generator output on or off, or queries its status.
params: 1 to the number of generators on the model; omitted = 1
remarks: - These commands require a built-in generator. On a model without one, every :SOURce command generates error -241,"Hardware missing". The settings drive the physical generator output.
- <n> addresses that generator directly, whichever generator is shown in the UI.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` or `0`.
commands.example:
:SOUR1:OUTP ON    /*Turns on the output of generator 1.*/
:SOUR1:OUTP?    /*The query returns 1.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the output waveform shape.
params: 1 to the number of generators on the model; omitted = 1
remarks: - These commands require a built-in generator. On a model without one, every :SOURce command generates error -241,"Hardware missing". The settings drive the physical generator output.
commands.returns: The query returns SIN, SQU, RAMP, PULS, NOIS, DC or ARB.
commands.example:
:SOUR:FUNC SQU    /*Selects a square wave.*/
:SOUR:FUNC?    /*The query returns SQU.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the duty cycle of the square and pulse waveforms in percent. Values outside the range are clipped to the range limit.
params: 1 to the number of generators on the model; omitted = 1
remarks: - These commands require a built-in generator. On a model without one, every :SOURce command generates error -241,"Hardware missing". The settings drive the physical generator output.
commands.returns: The query returns the duty cycle in a real number in scientific notation with seven significant digits (for example `1.000000E+00`); `9.9E37` when the value is unavailable.
commands.example:
:SOUR:FUNC:SQU:DUTY 25    /*Sets 25 % duty.*/
:SOUR:FUNC:SQU:DUTY?    /*The query returns 2.500000E+01.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the symmetry of the ramp waveform in percent. Values outside the range are clipped to the range limit.
params: 1 to the number of generators on the model; omitted = 1
remarks: - These commands require a built-in generator. On a model without one, every :SOURce command generates error -241,"Hardware missing". The settings drive the physical generator output.
commands.returns: The query returns the symmetry in a real number in scientific notation with seven significant digits (for example `1.000000E+00`); `9.9E37` when the value is unavailable.
commands.example:
:SOUR:FUNC:RAMP:SYMM 80    /*Sets 80 % symmetry.*/
:SOUR:FUNC:RAMP:SYMM?    /*The query returns 8.000000E+01.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the output frequency in Hz. The value is limited to the range the generator supports for the current waveform shape; read it back to obtain the applied value.
params: 1 to the number of generators on the model; omitted = 1
Depends on the model and waveform shape
remarks: - These commands require a built-in generator. On a model without one, every :SOURce command generates error -241,"Hardware missing". The settings drive the physical generator output.
commands.returns: The query returns the frequency in a real number in scientific notation with seven significant digits (for example `1.000000E+00`); `9.9E37` when the value is unavailable.
commands.example:
:SOUR:FREQ 10000    /*Sets 10 kHz.*/
:SOUR:FREQ?    /*The query returns 1.000000E+04.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the output amplitude in Vpp. The value is limited to what the generator supports at the current frequency; read it back to obtain the applied value.
params: 1 to the number of generators on the model; omitted = 1
Depends on the model and frequency
remarks: - These commands require a built-in generator. On a model without one, every :SOURce command generates error -241,"Hardware missing". The settings drive the physical generator output.
commands.returns: The query returns the amplitude in a real number in scientific notation with seven significant digits (for example `1.000000E+00`); `9.9E37` when the value is unavailable.
commands.example:
:SOUR:VOLT 2    /*Sets 2 Vpp.*/
:SOUR:VOLT?    /*The query returns 2.000000E+00.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the DC offset of the output in volts. The value is limited to what the generator supports; for the DC shape the range is -5 V to 5 V.
params: 1 to the number of generators on the model; omitted = 1
Depends on the model and amplitude
remarks: - These commands require a built-in generator. On a model without one, every :SOURce command generates error -241,"Hardware missing". The settings drive the physical generator output.
commands.returns: The query returns the offset in a real number in scientific notation with seven significant digits (for example `1.000000E+00`); `9.9E37` when the value is unavailable.
commands.example:
:SOUR:VOLT:OFFS 0.5    /*Sets a 500 mV offset.*/
:SOUR:VOLT:OFFS?    /*The query returns 5.000000E-01.*/

commands.desc: Loads one period of an arbitrary waveform as a list of samples and selects the ARB shape. The samples may have any scale; non-numeric entries are skipped.
params: 1 to the number of generators on the model; omitted = 1
remarks: - These commands require a built-in generator. On a model without one, every :SOURce command generates error -241,"Hardware missing". The settings drive the physical generator output.
- If the generator does not accept the list (for example too few samples), the command generates error -224,"Illegal parameter value" <count> samples.
- There is no query form; :SOURce:ARB:DATA? generates error -113,"Undefined header".
commands.example: :SOUR:ARB:DATA 0,0.5,1,0.5,0,-0.5,-1,-0.5    /*Loads an 8-point triangle period.*/

commands.desc: Uses the on-screen record of the specified channel as one period of the arbitrary waveform. The captured waveform is also saved as arb.csv on the instrument.
params: 1 to the number of generators on the model; omitted = 1
remarks: - These commands require a built-in generator. On a model without one, every :SOURce command generates error -241,"Hardware missing". The settings drive the physical generator output.
- If the channel has no usable record, the command generates error -224 with the reason.
commands.example: :SOUR:ARB:CAPT CHAN1    /*Replays the CH1 screen as the ARB waveform.*/

commands.desc: Turns modulation on or off, or queries its status. Turning it on keeps the current modulation type, or selects AM if none is set.
params: 1 to the number of generators on the model; omitted = 1
remarks: - These commands require a built-in generator. On a model without one, every :SOURce command generates error -241,"Hardware missing". The settings drive the physical generator output.
commands.returns: The query returns `1` or `0`.
commands.example:
:SOUR:MOD ON    /*Turns on modulation.*/
:SOUR:MOD?    /*The query returns 1.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the modulation type. Selecting a type also turns modulation on.
params: 1 to the number of generators on the model; omitted = 1
remarks: - These commands require a built-in generator. On a model without one, every :SOURce command generates error -241,"Hardware missing". The settings drive the physical generator output.
commands.returns: The query returns NONE, AM, FM or PM. NONE means that modulation is off.
commands.example:
:SOUR:MOD:TYP FM    /*Selects frequency modulation.*/
:SOUR:MOD:TYP?    /*The query returns FM.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the AM depth in percent. Values outside the range are clipped to the range limit.
params: 1 to the number of generators on the model; omitted = 1
remarks: - These commands require a built-in generator. On a model without one, every :SOURce command generates error -241,"Hardware missing". The settings drive the physical generator output.
commands.returns: The query returns the depth in a real number in scientific notation with seven significant digits (for example `1.000000E+00`); `9.9E37` when the value is unavailable.
commands.example:
:SOUR:MOD:AM:DEPT 50    /*Sets 50 % AM depth.*/
:SOUR:MOD:AM:DEPT?    /*The query returns 5.000000E+01.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the FM frequency deviation in Hz. Values below 0.01 Hz are raised to 0.01 Hz.
params: 1 to the number of generators on the model; omitted = 1
remarks: - These commands require a built-in generator. On a model without one, every :SOURce command generates error -241,"Hardware missing". The settings drive the physical generator output.
commands.returns: The query returns the deviation in a real number in scientific notation with seven significant digits (for example `1.000000E+00`); `9.9E37` when the value is unavailable.
commands.example:
:SOUR:MOD:FM:DEV 500    /*Sets 500 Hz deviation.*/
:SOUR:MOD:FM:DEV?    /*The query returns 5.000000E+02.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the PM phase deviation in degrees. Values outside the range are clipped to the range limit.
params: 1 to the number of generators on the model; omitted = 1
remarks: - These commands require a built-in generator. On a model without one, every :SOURce command generates error -241,"Hardware missing". The settings drive the physical generator output.
commands.returns: The query returns the deviation in a real number in scientific notation with seven significant digits (for example `1.000000E+00`); `9.9E37` when the value is unavailable.
commands.example:
:SOUR:MOD:PM:DEV 45    /*Sets 45 degrees deviation.*/
:SOUR:MOD:PM:DEV?    /*The query returns 4.500000E+01.*/

commands.desc: Sets or queries the frequency of the internal modulating waveform in Hz. One value is shared by AM, FM and PM, so <type> may be any of them. Values outside the range are clipped to the range limit.
params: 1 to the number of generators on the model; omitted = 1
remarks: - These commands require a built-in generator. On a model without one, every :SOURce command generates error -241,"Hardware missing". The settings drive the physical generator output.
commands.returns: The query returns the frequency in a real number in scientific notation with seven significant digits (for example `1.000000E+00`); `9.9E37` when the value is unavailable.
commands.example:
:SOUR:MOD:AM:INT:FREQ 1000    /*Sets a 1 kHz modulating frequency.*/
:SOUR:MOD:AM:INT:FREQ?    /*The query returns 1.000000E+03.*/

params: 1 to the number of generators on the model; omitted = 1
remarks: - These commands require a built-in generator. On a model without one, every :SOURce command generates error -241,"Hardware missing". The settings drive the physical generator output.

commands.example:
:SOUR:MOD:AM:INT:FUNC TRI    /*Modulates with a triangle.*/
:SOUR:MOD:AM:INT:FUNC?    /*The query returns TRI.*/

subsystems.title: Calibration and Identification Commands
subsystems.intro: The :CALibrate commands run the self-calibration of the analog front end. The :IDENtify? query runs automatic signal identification on the current record. Neither is a passive read.

commands.desc: Starts self-calibration of the specified channel, or of all channels when <ch> is 0. The optional ZERO keyword selects the zero-offset calibration option. Calibration runs in the background; poll :CALibrate:STATus?.
params: 0 to 4 (0 = all channels; larger values are treated as 4, non-numeric values as 0)
remarks: - Disconnect all signals from the inputs before starting. Calibration changes the stored calibration data and is not a passive diagnostic.
- Calibration requires the hardware acquisition source; with a file or simulated source, :CALibrate:STATus? reports that hardware is needed.
- The command does not report errors; check :CALibrate:STATus?.
commands.example:
:CAL:STAR 0    /*Starts self-calibration of all channels.*/
:CAL:STAR 2,ZERO    /*Starts calibration of CH2 with the zero option.*/

commands.desc: Cancels a running self-calibration.
commands.example: :CAL:CANC    /*Cancels the self-calibration in progress.*/

commands.desc: Queries the status of the self-calibration.
commands.returns: The query returns a free-text status line: `idle`, `starting ...`, `<percent> % <step>` while running, `done: <summary>` or `failed: <reason>` after a run, or `needs the hardware source` when calibration is not possible.
commands.example: :CAL:STAT?    /*The query returns 42 % CH2 offset.*/

commands.desc: Runs signal identification on the current record of the channels that are on and returns the findings. The query also updates the identification shown in the UI.
remarks: - This query is not passive: it starts an analysis and may show a message on the screen.
commands.returns: The query returns the findings separated by `;`, each in the format `CH<a>[+CH<b>] <summary> (<confidence> %)`. It returns an empty line when nothing is found.
commands.example: :IDEN?    /*The query returns CH1 Clock 1.000 kHz (90 %).*/

subsystems.title: :SYSTem Commands
subsystems.intro: The :SYSTem commands read the error queue, give direct access to every setting stored in a setup file, report diagnostic state and control the measurement logger.

commands.desc: Queries and removes the oldest entry of the error queue. Read repeatedly until `0,"No error"` is returned.
remarks: - The queue holds up to 20 entries of at most 256 bytes each; when it overflows, error -350 is queued.
- Typical codes: -113 undefined header, -221 settings conflict, -224 illegal parameter value, -230 data unavailable, -241 hardware missing, -256 file name not found.
commands.returns: The query returns `<code>,"<message>"`, optionally followed by a space and detail text, for example `-113,"Undefined header" :FOO`.
commands.example: :SYST:ERR?    /*The query returns 0,"No error".*/

commands.desc: Writes one setup-file setting on the live instrument, using the same key and value syntax as a saved setup file. This gives access to settings that have no dedicated command.
params: A setup key, an equals sign and its value
remarks: - Keys and value formats are those of the OOS setup file and may change between versions; read the current value with :SYSTem:GET? before writing.

- Useful keys include `tdiv` (s/div), `ch1.vdiv` (V/div), `ch1.on` (`true`/`false`), `math_expr<n>` (formula of math trace n), `eye` (`<source> <bit rate> <rate from record 0|1>`; bit rate 0 = measured) and `eye_more` (eight fields: BER target, two frequency limits, three flags and sources, where the seventh field is the eye clock/strobe source, `-` for none).
- A missing `=`, an invalid value or an unknown key generates error -224,"Illegal parameter value" (for example `unknown key <key>`).
commands.example:
:SYST:SET eye = R2 0 1    /*Eye of R2, bit rate measured from the whole record.*/
:SYST:SET eye_more = 0.000000000001 1000 1000000 0 - 0 R1 1    /*Folds the eye on the strobe in R1.*/

commands.desc: Queries the current value of one setup-file setting.
remarks: - Keys that are only stored when they differ from their default (for example `ch1.label`) return an empty reply while at the default.
commands.returns: The query returns the value text exactly as it appears in a setup file; it returns an empty line for an unknown key.
commands.example: :SYST:GET? eye    /*The query returns R2 0 1.*/

commands.desc: Queries one line of diagnostic state: frame rate and counters, run state, trigger status and timing figures.
commands.returns: The query returns a single line in the format `fps <f> frames <n> records <n> run <Run|Stop> status <status> t <s> step <ms> ms (acq <ms> draw <ms>) render <ms> ms present <ms> ms edges <a> <b> <c> <d> off <x> <y>`.
commands.example: :SYST:STAT?    /*The query returns one diagnostic line beginning with fps.*/

commands.desc: Starts or stops the measurement logger. When started, the current measurement readouts are written to a new CSV log file in the save directory of the instrument.
remarks: - The logger does not start when no measurement is active; a message is shown instead.
- The log file is written on the instrument running OOS, not on the remote client.
commands.example: :SYST:LOG ON    /*Starts logging the measurements.*/
